With the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) fixing a tariff of Rs 15.96 per unit for power through solar energy, the state government is confident of attracting top corporate houses to set up solar power plants in Haryana.

Being the fourth state after Rajasthan, Punjab and West Bengal to announce tariffs for power generation through solar energy, Haryana is hopeful of leading the race with maximum tariffs. Reliance Industries Ltd., Albina Power, ACME Telepower, Epuron Renewable Energy Power, Emco, RS India Wind Energy and Admire Energy Solutions (Moser Baer Company) etc. have already evinced interest in producing power from solar energy in Haryana, says Sumita Misra, Director of HAREDA.

The state government is also promoting the use of the energy-saving CFLs in a big way. "By 2010, Haryana will become self reliant in power. Besides the addition of around 3300 MW of power through various plants under construction, we will get around 4000 MW from power purchase agreements. But the state is also going for alternative sources of power," said Haryana Power Minister Randeep Singh Surjewala.

Heading: For tourists, Gorkha body gives 60-hr break from bandh - Indian Express
Content:
It has been raining in Pilupura for the last two days and the Jogis of Jogi Ka Kalan village have been itching to pick their ploughs, harness the bulls and set out to start tilling their land. But for now, they can only wait and hope the Gurjjars, who have been camping on their land, wind up their agitation so that they can sow their bajra.

"Gurjjaro ne kaha hai ki yahan arkashan ka beej pehle boyega, phir bajra (Gurjjars have said that the seeds of reservations will be sowed here first and then bajra)," said 60-year-old Joti, pointing to the manure and seeds piled on his verandah. He and his seven brothers own around 20 bhigas in the area.

Jogi Ka Kalan village is a few meters away from ground zero of the Gurjjar agitation. The village has predominantly Jogi families, though some decades ago, a few Gurjjar families settled here.

"After Diwali, we sow wheat but bajra supplements our income. We don't know when the Gurjjars will leave our fields. We don't dare ask them either," said Puran, another landowner in the village.

The Gurjjar diktat for its community members is clear too. No one will start working on their fields till the state government sends the recommendation letter for ST status to the Centre. Anyone who tries to work will have to pay a penalty of Rs 1,100.

For the last 18 days, Jogi Ka Kalan has no electricity. The government cut supply to all 84 villages in the area to punish the agitating Gurjjars. Electricity was restored only after Monday's first round of talks between Gurjjars and the government ended peacefully in Bayana.

Jogis, like the Gurjjars, are OBCs and share the grouse the Gurjjars hold towards the Meenas who enjoy ST status. Though Meenas have kept out of this year's agitation, the Jogis are quick to point out how the Meenas have been benefited from reservation. "No one in the village goes to college. But what is the point? Even if our children score 90 per cent they do not have a future. There are no jobs for us," Joti said.

"Our lives have been paralysed for the last 18 days. But the Gurjjars have every right to protest," said Ramji Lal, another villager.

Heading: No talks in Jaipur, Gurjjars ensure Bainsla stays put - Indian Express
Content:
Forty eight hours after their call for an indefinite bandh, the Gorkha Janmukti Manch on Wednesday announced a 60-hour relaxation to give passage to tourists who were stranded in Darjeeling.

GJM president Bimal Gurung, who had called the bandh after the police and CPI(M) cadres assaulted his supporters during a protest in Siliguri, said tourists were "guests" and his party's agitation would follow the non-violent path towards its goal for a separate state in Gorkhaland.

"We are not targeting the tourists here," Gurung told The Indian Express. "Those who are still stranded in Darjeeling, Dooars, Kalimpong and other areas are being treated as guests. We will help them get 50 per cent discount in hotels, apart from helping them financially if they have spent their money. For those who want to leave the hills, we will arrange for vehicles," he said.

While the Darjeeling hills remained peaceful, group clashes were reported from Malbazar and Oldabari in the Dooars. Around 3.30pm, Bengalis clashed with Nepali GJM supporters at Malbazar when GJM activists tried to enforce the bandh. A petrol pump was ransacked and around six people were injured. A huge contingent of police was rushed to the area. At nearby Oldabari, GJM vehicles were burnt down by anti-bandh supporters.

Meanwhile, the state government asked the Centre for additional six companies of CRPF and rushed them to Siliguri. According to police sources, a decision on CRPF's deployment in and around Darjeeling is awaited. The GJM on its part faxed memorandums to PM Manmohan Singh and Home Minister Shivraj Patil, asking them to stop sending paramilitary forces, as this would heighten tension in the area.

"This is our final agitation for a separate state. So far, our supporters have engaged in peaceful agitations but the CPI(M) is provoking them," said Gurung. He said deployment of the CRPF is a useless exercise. "It will only add to the tension," he said.

Darjeeling and adjacent areas remained shut down for the third consecutive day because of the strike. Road link to Sikkim was cut off as GJM supporters blocked NH-31.

KL Tamta, Inspector General Of Police of north Bengal said GJM supporters are not allowing government vehicles to ply in Darjeeling and surrounding areas. "There was a rail blockade by GJM supporters in the morning but was cleared soon after," Tamta said.

Heading: Her own partymen put spoke in Raje’s wheels - Indian Express
Content:
The deadlock over further talks between agitating Gurjjars and the Rajasthan Government remained on Wednesday with leader of the agitators Kirori Singh Bainsla sticking to his precondition of the release of women protestors who were arrested from Dausa district.

A bail plea of the 25 arrested women has been rejected by magistrate. A fresh application would be presented on Thursday for their release. The state Government has made it clear that the case is beyond its reach. "The women are under judicial custody and their release will be decided by court alone. We cannot do much about it," said Principal Secretary S N Thanvi.

Meanwhile, the Jaipur police arrested 70 Gurjjars under Section 107/51. There are more than thousand Gurjjar men and women under arrest in Rajasthan.

The Gurjjars have formed a 21-member team. "We are ready and as soon as the Government releases the women, we will be ready to go to Jaipur for second round of talks," Bainsla said here. Besides the release of the women arrested for damaging a rail track in stir-hit Dausa district, he demanded the release of men taken into custody in the wake of the agitation and restoration of electricity and water and jammed telecommunication network in the agitation-affected areas.

Wednesday saw differences between Bainsla and other Gurjjar leaders widening. While the retired Colonel has been suggesting for the past two days that only talks can resolve the issue, the others are adamant that Bainsla would not be leaving for any preliminary talks till the Government gave a clear indication that the recommendation letter would be sent.

Sources said Bainsla himself had told Thanvi that he was ready to go for talks in Jaipur.

At the camp in Pilupura, there were signs of growing weariness among the agitating Gurjjars. The womenfolk stayed away from the spot on Wednesday. The number of agitators has also dwindled by a few thousands. Piles of garbage and human refuse are piling around the area. "We need to hire sweepers immediately. We request all of you to bring them from your villages," senior Gurjjar leader Attar Singh was heard announcing repeatedly.

Twentieth day into agitation, Bainsla's wit however remains intact. Congratulating Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav on his birthday, he said, "I am thankful to Laluji for having allowed us to stay on railway line for the past 20 days to lodge our protest against the Government. I wish him happy birthday." Bainsla also penned a short poem in Hindi for Lalu's birthday.

Heading: ‘Afzal is 27th on 28 pending mercy pleas’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Vasundhara Raje Government is caught in a cleft stick with agitating Gurjjars on one hand imposing preconditions for dialogue and on the other, the local BJP, with tacit outside support, forcing the normally tough Chief Minister to negotiate with Kirori Singh Bainsla and his band to prevent any political fallout in western Uttar Pradesh.

While Raje would like to be tough on any untoward law and order situation created by militant Gurjjars, the state BJP chief and party veteran O P Mathur and Prakash Javdekar, the self-appointed emissary of party president Rajnath Singh, have a different view on how to solve the ongoing agitation. State unit prabhari Gopinath Munde, who apparently is with Raje on solving the crisis without a loss of face, chooses to remain silent given the political clout of the other two BJP leaders.

And before the present logjam was sorted out for a dialogue between Bainsla and the state Government, the former imposed the precondition of releasing the arrested Gurjjar women. Apparently, Raje was so unhappy about the precondition that she was in favour of writing a strongly worded letter to Bainsla as releasing the women, arrested under substantive sections of the IPC and CrPC, meant that the state Government would lose face even before the talks began. However, the idea of such a letter was shot down by the state unit chief and Javdekar, who wanted resolution of crisis imediately at any cost. The state Government has already written five letters to Bainsla inviting him for talks.

Although an influential section of the BJP thinks that Raje should adopt a tough stand with agitating Gurjjars as the growing assessment is that it is the lumpens and not Bainsla who are in control of the movement. But this view is countered by another section that believes the party's poll prospects would be damaged in neighbouring states with a strong Gurjjar presence in Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh. Added to this is the fact that BJP chief Rajnath Singh has plans to contest the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections from Ghaziabad, which has a sizable Gurjjar population.

Heading: India, US sort differences on VVIP jet deal - Indian Express
Content:
Going by the ruling Congress' argument, a decision on Parliament House attack convict Afzal Guru's clemency petition could take much longer. The ruling party on Wednesday said Afzal's petition was 27th in the list of 28 and the Government could take a decision only in the order in which they were filed.

"Afzal's petition is 27th. Law will take its own course. The petitions that were filed earlier will obviously have to be heard earlier. That's what the law says," All India Congress Committee spokesperson Manish Tewari said at a press briefing.

The Congress also sought to turn the table on the BJP for accusing the ruling party of minority appeasement in this context. "The BJP is accusing the UPA of appeasement. Does the BJP think 194 million Muslims are anti-nationals that they will get appeased if Afzal is not hanged?

Muslims as any other community had felt the same sense of outrage at the attack on Parliament. What Afzal has been convicted for is unpardonable, but law has to take its own course," said Tewari.

"The petitions have to be disposed of in the order that they were filed because India is not a banana republic.

India has a very strong rule of law," he added. Out of 28 petitions, 1 has been pending since 1997, while 15 others came during the NDA regime, said the Congress spokesperson.

Heading: Relief package for Bhagalpur riots on Cabinet agenda today - Indian Express
Content:
Ending all speculation, India and the US have resolved differences over a contentious end user verification law that threatened to come in the way of a deal to procure missile protection systems for Indian VVIP aircraft.

After weeks of deliberations, the two sides have agreed on a new end user verification agreement that negates the need for physical verification of the sensitive systems and relies on written assurances given by the Indian Air Force (IAF).

The $40 million deal to procure AN/AAQ-24 LAIRCM (Large Aircraft Infra Red Countermeasure Systems) for three Indian VVIP Business Boeing Jets entered muddy waters earlier this year, after India refused to sign a 'compulsory' agreement that would permit periodic physical verification of the systems by US inspectors.

While US argued that physical inspection of systems was mandatory by their laws and was needed to ensure that the technology did not fall into wrong hands, India had argued that as a sovereign nation, it could not allow inspections and offered access to records and written assurances.

MoD sources said the matter has now been resolved through a new end user verification agreement. Earlier, the missile protection system was being procured through a country to country agreement (Foreign Military Sale) that would mandate physical inspection of the systems due to US defence export laws.

To work things around this compulsory clause, the systems will now be purchased directly by the IAF from US-based Northrop Grumman that manufactures the systems. Sources say the company to company agreement would do away with the need to physical verification as the US firm would take responsibility for 'correct usage' of the missile protection systems.

Confirming that the issue has been resolved, US embassy officials said the three VVIP Business Boeing Jets are shortly expected to reach India. "We anticipate that the aircraft will be delivered shortly with al the equipment that India desires," said a US Embassy official.

MoD officials say the US was being extra sensitive regarding the transfer as the missile protection system is new and has only been offered to the UK, Canada and India. A similar system is fitted on board the US President Air Force One and security of a number of top officials could be compromised if information on the system is leaked.

However, with all issues resolved, the three aircraft would be arriving in New Delhi by July-end, only a month behind schedule. The delay, officials say, is due to last minute issues in integrating a few systems on the VVIP jets.

India had inked a Rs 937-crore deal in 2005 to acquire three Boeing Business Jets for VVIP travel. The deal included a $40 million US foreign military sale for three aircraft self protection systems - AN/AAQ-24 LAIRCM (Large Aircraft Infra Red Countermeasure System), AN/ALE-47H countermeasure dispensing systems and AN/ALQ-211 early warning suite controller and radar warning systems.

Heading: SC raps rape convict for sharing name with Nehru - Indian Express
Content:
Less than a month after it cleared a relief package to victims of the 2002 communal riots in Gujarat, the UPA Government is all set to announce a similar package for victims of the 1989 Bhagalpur riots in Bihar. The Union Cabinet, which is scheduled to meet on Thursday, is likely to consider a proposal moved by the Home Ministry in this regard.

Sources said the proposed package for Bhagalpur riots victims will be at par with that offered to victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. The same measures were adopted for the Gujarat riots' relief package.

Under the package, the victims whose residential properties had been damaged are likely to get an additional ex gratia of 10 times the amount given by the state Government minus the amount already paid by the state.

The move follows BJP's criticisms of the UPA Government for announcing a relief package for victims of the Gujarat riots with an eye on general elections but ignored those of the Bhagalpur riots even though the state was then under Congress rule.

In fact, Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar had earlier written a letter to the Prime Minister asking for a relief package for the victims of the Bhagalpur riots at par with those of the anti-Sikh riots. After coming to power in Bihar, Nitish had constituted a commission of inquiry under Justice N N Singh, which had recommended a relief package at par with the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), which is also slated to meet on Thursday, is likely to consider fixing minimum support price (MSP) for the forthcoming kharif crop season.

Heading: Akhilesh puts it in words: ‘Cong-SP ties only natural’ - Indian Express
Content:
What's in a name? Shakespeare may have thought that way but the Supreme Court on Wednesday thought otherwise when it expressed its annoyance that a convict, accused of raping a minor girl, shared his name with the late Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.

"You have committed a rape and share the name with Jawaharlal Nehru. It is a disgrace for the national ethos," observed a vacation Bench comprising Justices Arijit Pasayat and P P Naolekar. The Bench was hearing an appeal filed by convict Nehru alias Jawahar, who had challenged his conviction by the Madhya Pradesh High Court for the offence.

SC said such culprits sharing names with national leaders were a disgrace and added, "We think it is time we should do something on this issue."

Hearing advocate Shishir Pinaki, amicus curiae appointed by the court, the Bench reserved its verdict in the case. The amicus filed a report seeking acquittal of Nehru on the ground that there were several discrepancies in the prosecution's theory. He submitted that there were inaccuracies in the FIR and there was no medical evidence to corroborate the rape charge.

The court was further told that Nehru was falsely implicated by the victim and her mother as he had refused to buy firewood from them. According to the prosecution, Nehru in 1988 had raped the 16-year-old girl at Rajendra Nand Gaon in Chhattisgarh. While Sessions court sentenced him to seven years imprisonment, the Madhya Pradesh HC in 2001 reduced the sentence to five years. Nehru then filed an appeal in the apex court.

Heading: Deshmukh safe, heat on Alva, Rau - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress-SP thaw has just got another boost with Mulayam Singh Yadav's son and Kannauj MP in the Lok Sabha Akhilesh Yadav backing normalisation of ties between the parties. "Prime Minister Manmohan Singh gave Amar Singh uncle so much respect at the dinner (on the UPA Government completing four years in office) recently. If the ties between the two parties are improving, it's only to be welcomed," Akhilesh told The Indian Express on Wednesday.

With mutually exclusive social constituencies, a Congress-SP alliance is likely to be more durable then a Congress-BSP alliance (with the BSP eyeing Congress's social constituency). "They (the Congress) have realised that the BSP and Chief Minister Mayawati must be fought. The BSP has been our principal rival in the state. The convergence of interests, then, is only natural," said Akhilesh.

Asked if he would accept a similar invite from Rahul, the young MP said: "It's like tearing your hair over naming the child even before the marriage has been solemnised" and added: "All the decisions would be taken by netaji (Mulayam Singh Yadav) and Amar Singh uncle. With the leaders around, we (the youth brigade) will only follow."

The ties between the two parties have been improving steadily ever since SP general secretary Amar Singh gave an interview to a national weekly, describing Rahul as a "nice young man, who wrote him an emotional letter when his father passed away". The SP leader was later invited for a Rajiv Gandhi Foundation function, followed by the dinner at the PM's residence.

Singh has, however, maintained that the two parties are "neither friends nor enemies, even if the barbs from the Congress camp have stopped completely". Technically, the SP continues to be a constituent of the United National Progressive Alliance.

Refusing to attach too much significance to the recent Mayawati-Mulayam meeting in Lucknow, Akhilesh said "our (anti-BSP) roadmap in UP is very clear". While in the past the young SP MP has taken digs at the Congress heir, his statements now clearly show the rapidly changing political alignments in Uttar Pradesh.

While Rahul Gandhi is known to believe in reviving the party "by going it alone in the crucial state of Uttar Pradesh", many state leaders don't rule out an alliance as "a short-term measure".

For the SP, too, normalisation of ties with the Congress is more than welcome, especially in view of Mayawati's "blow hot, blow cold policy" towards the party's first family and Amar Singh.

Heading: After a fatherly no, Karunanidhi has dad of all b’days - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh looks set to continue with the Congress high command on Wednesday asking him to focus on the ensuing Assembly and Lok Sabha elections. While the NCP is also said to have conveyed its reservation about a change of guard in the state at this stage, it was the TINA (There Is No Alternative) factor that swung in favour of Deshmukh.

The heat is now on AICC general secretary in charge of Maharashtra Margaret Alva and PCC chief Prabha Rau who were gunning for Deshmukh citing his lacklustre performance. Efforts are also on to placate the CM's bete noire Narayan Rane who has been offered the post of Election Campaign Committee head, similar to the one given to former Karnataka CM S M Krishna upon his return to politics. Rane is yet to accept the offer though, according to his close aides.

Alva is likely to be divested of the charge of Maharashtra in an organisational reshuffle, expected to be effected after the A K Antony committee submits its report on the roadmap for the party for the ensuing elections, according to party sources. The leadership is also looking for a Dalit face to replace Rau as PCC chief. AICC general secretary Mukul Wasnik is said to be one of the contenders for the post.

While Union Power Minister Sushilkumar Shinde was till recently in the reckoning for the CM's post, what went against him was the general perception that he lacked the stature and appeal to influence cross sections of voters.

Heading: Maharajganj: Maya sacks SHO, doctor - Indian Express
Content:
For A man who protested that he didn't want his birthday celebrated, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M Karunanidhi is certainly having his cake and eating it too.

The grand statewide celebrations which began on June 3 were only the curtain-raiser for a party that is to last a month in Tamil Nadu. Across the state, the jubilation is continuing: from the cricket pitches in Chennai to fields in the districts.

Off the sporting arena, a university has decided to translate Karunanidhi's works from Tamil to English for the benefit of hundreds of non-Tamilians. Eighty-five of his literary works — Karunanidhi turned 85 on June 3 — were released in Chennai on Tuesday.

The grandest tribute is underway in Chennai: a cricket tournament for the Kalaignar Gold Cup. Inaugurated on June 6 by state Electricity Minister and senior DMK leader Arcot N Veerasamy, the tourney has 50 matches every day, played under lights from 6.30 pm till early morning at five grounds in the city, with 1,285 teams participating. The 10-over per side tournament is played with a tennis ball and has no registration fee.

Helping out is N Srinivasan, a prominent face in cricket administration and the Managing Director of India Cements, which owns the IPL team Chennai Super Kings.

"A team has to play seven rounds before clinching a berth in the quarter finals," says J Anbazhagan, the South Chennai DMK secretary and organiser of the Kalaignar Gold Cup.

Just in case anyone misses the point, members of all teams have received T-shirts with Karunanidhi's photograph.

The final will be held on July 6, exactly a month after the tournament began. Anbazhagan says they are trying to assemble all the prominent cricketers of the state, who have played the game at the top levels.

However, the fun isn't just restricted to cricket. "From June 17, other games like football, volleyball and kabaddi will begin," Anbazhagan says.

There is no let-up in the festivities in villages either, though the form is different. Earlier this week, about 100 bullock carts took part in a race in Madurai.

Meanwhile, Bharathiar University, Coimbatore, has announced the translation of as many as 100 literary works by the Chief Minister from Tamil to English. To add to the festive mood, the Vice-Chancellor said doctoral and M.Phil theses could be prepared in Tamil, with the best writer getting a 'Dr Kalaignar Science Award'.

Heading: Cong: Modi statement smacks of treason - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati on Wednesday asked senior police officers in the state to stop "selling" posts of station house officers. Warning of strict action against erring officers, she said this system prevented the poor from getting proper justice.

The CM, addressing a meeting of IGs ad DIGs, called to review the law and order situation in the state, also directed Principal Secretary (Home) Kunawar Fateh Bahadur and DGP Vikram Singh to tour the state and put an end to corruption in the Police Department. "Any sort of bargaining for the posting of police officers is unforgivable," the CM said.

The CM said the Maharjganj incident, involving former fisheries minister Jamuna Prasad Nishad, could have been averted had the police acted on time. She also announced the decision to dismiss the Maharajganj Sadar Kotwali SHO and the medical officer of the district for their handling of the situation. Maharajganj District Magistrate S P Dixit has meanwhile been shifted to Mirzapur.

Heading: Rio Govt sees music as way out of violence - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress on Wednesday sensed "treason" in Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on Sunday that the Centre, if it so wishes, need not pay anything to Gujarat for a year but then it should also not collect any taxes from the state.

Condemning his remarks, AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari said the statement was an "assault on the idea of India". "This statement smells of treason," he said at a press briefing here.

At a function in Vadodara on Sunday, Modi had said that the Centre collects around Rs 40,000 crore by way of taxes from Gujarat, but gives only 2.5 per cent of central funds to the state. If the Centre so wishes, it need not pay anything to Gujarat for a year but should also not collect any taxes from the state, the CM was reported to have said.

"The BJP has to state whether it agrees to what he says. Is this their concept of Akhand Bharat? No CM has ever said he will not give taxes to the Central Government. Instead of filing a treason case against journalists, it should be registered against Modi," said Tewari. Asked if the Congress was preparing to file such a case, he said, "The Congress will not hesitate to do anything in the interest of the country."

However, the BJP chose to downplay Modi's remarks, saying it was an expression of "agony over step-motherly treatment" meted out to the state. "Modi was showing his agony. He felt concerned over the step-motherly treatment meted out by the Centre. It was not a policy statement," Venkaiah Naidu said.

Heading: With 64 men dead, ULFA on the run ‘like never before’ - Indian Express
Content:
After more than six decades of insurgency and gun-culture spoiling the lives of thousands of Nagas, the Neiphiu Rio Government has identified music as the new mantra to help young Nagas find both employment and a better life. A Special Task Force for Music is already in place since 2004 with the state Government also setting up a Centre of Excellence for Music and Performing Arts at Jotsoma near here, which, with music labs, seminar halls, recording studios, library is all set to churn out batches of young Naga musicians from 2009.

"The Government is of the opinion that music, though primarily a hobby, can be easily turned into a well-rewarding profession, and this, in turn, can provide employment opportunities to hundreds of talented young people," G Sema, project director of the Music Task Force, said.

Sema said traditionally, every Naga grows up with music. "Every Naga boy or girl can sing and play one or the other musical instrument. The Government is trying to institutionalise this tradition and provide them with a formal degree or diploma so that this can help them find new careers," Sema said.

Groups of interested students have gone on exposure trips to various cities of the country where they have participated in musical programmes. The Hornbill Festival, the annual tourism festival of Nagaland held every December, has also become a major venue for talent hunting. "The hotel industry alone requires hundreds of musicians, and we also plan to target that sector," Sema added.

Meanwhile, Kohima is preparing to host the 23rd annual convention of Spic-Macay from Monday, with the organisers expecting a turnout of over 500 students. "We are hosting renowned musicians like Hari Prasad Chaurasia, Vishwamohan Bhatt, Prabhat Sharma, Ghanakanta Bora and Fahimuddin Dagar who will perform as well as give lecture-demonstrations during the six-day event," said Prof K Kannan, Vice-Chancellor of Nagaland University, who is also a governing body member of Spic-Macay. Kannan added that these eminent artists would also get to hear traditional and folk music of the different Naga tribes, which, in turn, is expected to create new avenues for tribal music.

Heading: Now, fuel crunch takes toll on Kalpakkam unit - Indian Express
Content:
With the killing of Madhurjya Gohain, a self-styled Lieutenant of the 'C' company of ULFA's 28th Battalion, in an encounter on Tuesday, the outfit has lost as many as 64 cadres in less than six months. According to the security forces, this has severely hit the activities of the outfit in the region. "ULFA's moral is at an all-time low. It has lost 64 cadres since January, while 182 of its members have surrendered to security forces during the same period," a spokesperson at the Army's Four Corps headquarters in Tezpur said on Wednesday.

Altogether, 11 ULFA cadres have been killed in the current month at the hands of security forces. "In January alone, 16 ULFA militants were killed," the spokesman said. The counter-insurgency operations in the region were intensified after an officer, Captain S Choudhury of the Gorkha Regiment, was killed in an encounter with the outfit in Tinsukia in January.

The ULFA, meanwhile, in the recent issue of its mouthpiece Swadhinata, has accused the Government of totally closing down the peace process and resorting to indiscriminate killings with the intention of eliminating the outfit through "gross violation" of human rights.

Heading: Panel: UGC, AICTE not doing enough to check ragging - Indian Express
Content:
After fuel shortage forced Nuclear Power Corporation of India to delay commissioning of new units at Kaiga Atomic Power Station and Rajasthan Atomic Power Station, NPCIL has admitted that because of fuel constraints it "may not be possible" to raise production levels at Madras Atomic Power Station in Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu. The Kalpakkam plant is one of the oldest nuclear power stations in the country.

NPCIL has, till now, never given a plant-wise indication on how fuel shortage has hit production levels of existing units and has officially termed the recent fall in plant load factor (PLF) of all nuclear power plants in the country on account of a general "mismatch" in the demand and supply of fuel. In a recent communiqué, however, NPCIL has put it on record that it would be unable to raise production levels at the 400 MW (two units of 220 MW each) Kalpakkam plant on account of fuel "constraints".

When asked by Southern Regional Power Committee on whether NPCIL can help in meeting the power demand of the region, NPCIL, apart from pointing out delay in commissioning of unit four in Kaiga in Karnataka, specifically stated that "with the constraints regarding fuel availability continuing, it may not be possible for us to raise generation from MAPS units".

NPCIL records illustrate how fuel shortage has hit production at their Kalpakkam plant. Production from unit one of Kalpakkam (220 MW, started in 1984) fell from a high 97 per cent capacity factor in 2003-04 to 72 per cent in 2006-07. Production from unit two (also 220 MW, started in 1986) which was at 77 per cent capacity factor in 2003-04 fell to 64 per cent in 2006-07. Interestingly, the availability factor of both these units during this period varied between 99 per cent and 86 per cent. What this means is that (taking unit one's performance in 2006-07), the unit is technically ready to generate 95 per cent of the capacity, but is only generating 72 per cent of the capacity. One of the possible reasons for this gap is fuel shortage.

On an average, the PLF of all nuclear plants has come down from a high 80 per cent to around 40 to 50 per cent on account of fuel shortage. Added to this, new units at Rajasthan APS (unit five and six) and Kaiga (unit four) are delayed because NPCIL does not have the required fuel.

Heading: Narmada canal breach floods villages - Indian Express
Content:
The University Grants Commission (UGC), All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and other educational regulatory bodies on Wednesday came under fire from the Raghavan committee, following the panel's findings that information on ragging incidents were not available with these agencies.

Sources said the Raghavan panel expressed disappointment over the helplessness shown by the apex bodies. The panel asked them to "link release of funds" to the "compliance on anti-ragging measures" for higher educational institutions.

"The release of grants under various schemes of the UGC should be linked with the compliance by institutions with the directions of the Supreme Court on ragging. Incentives by way of higher grants should be provided by the Commission to the higher educational institutions which ensure that ragging does not take place in their campuses in any form," a senior HRD official said.

Raghavan asked the regulatory bodies to prepare strict regulations to enforce anti-ragging measures in the higher educational institutions. He further asked the regulatory bodies to take necessary steps to ensure that educational institutions under their purview become zero tolerance campuses in respect of ragging.

The Committee also asked statutory regulatory bodies to direct educational institutions to incorporate appropriate messages regarding 'zero tolerance' towards 'ragging' in admission notices.

It said as the Supreme Court has upheld the recommendation that "ragging lowered the standards of higher education", each regulatory body responsible for maintaining standards of higher education was required to ensure that the directions of the apex court were strictly complied with. Wherever any incident of ragging is reported and institutions do not take adequate steps for redressing the grievance, regulatory bodies must conduct enquiries through fact finding committees, the Committee observed. It urged the Centre to take immediate steps to reinforce anti-ragging measures.

Heading: PLFI, the latest extremist threat in Chhattisgarh - Indian Express
Content:
Sujatpur village and nearby areas in Mehsana district was flooded on Wednesday due to a breach in the Narmada canal at Kadi. Rescue operations are on and villagers are being evacuated to safer places, the police said, adding that a probe is on to find the exact cause of the breach.

Among the six villages in the vicinity of the main canal, Sujatpura was the worst affected by the breach. The houses in the village, with a population of 2,100, were under three to four feet of water.

The other affected villages were Todmalpura, Bavjipura, Narsinhpura, Nani Kadi and Balasan. But water has started receding in these villages. A 30-member team, equipped with six boats drawn from the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, was engaged in rescue operations in the affected villages.

The state Government has decided to set up a high-powered technical committee to inquire into the circumstances that caused the breach. A comprehensive technical survey of the entire 458 km stretch of the main canal — from Kevadia to Rajasthan — will be undertaken to prevent such incidents in future.

After Chief Minister Narendra Modi visited the site on Wednesday, his ministers Nitin Patel, Narottam Patel and Amit Shah, former minister Bhupendrasinh Chudasma and senior officials of Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited rushed to the spot to oversee the rescue operations.

Addressing a press conference here on Wednesday evening, Health Minister Jay Narayan Vyas said the repairs of the 20-foot-wide breach on the main Narmada canal would be carried out on a war footing. The minister said the work is expected to be completed within the next 15 days. He conceded that drinking water supply was badly hit in villages like Radhanpur, Santalpur and other talukas of north Gujarat due to this incident.

The State Water Supply Board has been directed to make alternative arrangements for supplying potable water in these villages. He added that the high-powered committee would look into the exact causes of the breach. The committee would conduct a detailed study of hydrology, water pressure, soil bearing capacity and if the embankment was constructed as per specifications.

Responding to a query, he said the Government would initiate action against those found guilty. He, however, hastened to add that "there seems to be less chances of human error, if any, as the construction work on this portion of the main canal had been completed in 2003, and we are now into 2008".

Heading: J-K strike leaves thousands of tourists stranded - Indian Express
Content:
The Chhattisgarh Police is keeping a close watch on the relatively unknown Peoples' Liberation Front of India (PLFI), an outfit becoming active in the tribal Jashpur region, bordering Jharkhand, in the northern part of the state.

Posters of the extremist organisation first surfaced in Patratoli village, a forest area close to the border of Jharkhand's Simdega district. Soon, similar posters were seen in some other nearby villages, exhorting the people to raise their voice against "injustice, fight feudalism and capitalism" and also proclaiming that PLFI's aim was to establish a pro-people system.

Jashpur DSP Akbar Korram sought to downplay the threat saying, "It's not a Naxalite outfit, but a gang of criminals and extortionists". He said the Jharkhand Liberation Front (JLF), active in the neighbouring state, had rechristened itself as the PLFI under the leadership of one Dinesh Gop. He told The Indian Express over telephone that the police seized two PLFI posters about a fortnight ago, following which vigil has been stepped up in the area. "Patrolling has been intensified in all sensitive areas and all vehicles are being checked," he added.

Meanwhile, people in about half a dozen villages in the border areas of the district have already confirmed about the movement of armed PLFI cadres, who have been organising meetings to motivate unemployed youth to join them. It is suspected that these youth are being taken to the dense forests for training.

It has also come to notice of the authorities that PLFI cadres have started strengthening their cadre in Aara, Bansi, Portenga, Bhalmanda, Salekara and Bansi areas, with the support of some locals. In fact, some government contractors have abandoned their work and left these villages after PLFI cadres asked them to pay a "levy" for carrying out works in the area.

However, a district administration spokesman said none of the contractors have complained so far. "However, we will depute a team of officials to find out whether development initiatives, including construction of roads, are affected in any manner," he said, adding that adequate security would be provided if required.

Nearly two years ago, Naxalites had stormed a police outpost in Aara, killed two constables and looted weapons. Though Maoist cadres have their presence in the forests in Manora, Bagicha and Jashpur blocks of the districts, they apparently use this region as a safe haven as their activities are concentrated in neighbouring Sarguja district.

Earlier, the Maoist Communist Centre (MCC) and Peoples' War were active in the state's northern parts. After their merger, CPI (Maoist) now have considerable presence in over a dozen of the 18 districts.

Heading: Naxal violence on rise due to factional feud: Patil - Indian Express
Content:
With no commercial vehicles plying for the third consecutive day of the indefinite strike called by J-K transporters, over one lakh visitors are estimated to be stranded at various places across Jammu and Kashmir, as per the estimates from various quarters. The transporters are demanding a hike in passenger fares in the wake of the increase in the prices of petrol and diesel.

The strike has thrown life completely out of gear. Several Vaishno Devi pilgrims are stranded in Jammu and Katra, waiting in long queues for seats in the state-run SRTC vehicles, pressed into service since the day the strike started.

The pilgrims are complaining that the state Government is responsible for their plight since it did not make alternative arrangements despite knowing about the heavy rush of pilgrims to the state. "We had to wait for such a long time at Katra to get on to the SRTC bus and reach the station and proceed further. The state Government should have put more buses and opened more emergency ticket counters for the pilgrims. This state is in a total mess," said Sumesh Diwedi from New Delhi.

Heading: Rape victim’s suicide: 3 top cops, 21 lower officials shifted in Rohtak - Indian Express
Content:
Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Tuesday attributed the rise in extremist related incidents in Jharkhand to an increase in factional feuds rather than direct confrontations with security forces or civilians. Addressing a press conference here after touring Maoist-infested Daltongunj and Chatra towns, Patil observed that like in Nagaland, factional fight between extremist organisations were on the rise in Jharkhand too.

Asked if there was any possibility of a dialogue between the extremists and the Government, Patil said talks were possible if all sides agreed to it. He said the number of police stations and personnel in Naxalite-affected areas would be increased, adding that the police would be given sophisticated arms and better training. "They are trying to do their best. The morale of the security forces is high," he said. People thinking of grabbing power by the barrel of gun would never succeed as "our society seeks peaceful existence," he added.

The Home Minister ruled out the possibility of Maoists building up an international organisation in the backdrop of the development in Nepal.

Patil said states should have their own surrender policy and Jharkhand could also have one. "The Centre has been giving financial assistance to states to curb extremism, and will also assist in whatever way the states ask for," he said.

Heading: Gurjjars on warpath, Congress honours Rajesh Pilot - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after a 25-year-old woman committed suicide in the Haryana Police headquarters saying no action was being taken against two policemen who had raped her, Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Wednesday transferred three senior police officers for not taking timely action in the case.

Rohtak Range Inspector General Anil Dabra, District Superintendent of Police Hanief Qureshi and Deputy Superintendent of Police Dheeraj Setia have been transferred. Apart from them, 21 policemen deployed at the CIA (Central Investigation Authority) centre of the Rohtak police where the alleged rape took place have been shifted to police lines.

Inspector Ram Kumar, who was the investigating officer in the rape case, has been suspended while Head Constable Ramphal faces similar action, Haryana DGP Ranjiv Dalal told a press conference.

The large-scale action was an attempt by Hooda to contain the embarrassment to his government, particularly as Rohtak happens to be his home district.

Sarita was allegedly raped by Head Constable Balraj and Constable Silk Ram belonging to a CIA unit of the Rohtak police on April 10, and she committed suicide on June 9 expressing frustration that no action had been taken against the two. Since her suicide, the two are absconding and have been dismissed.

Earlier, Sarita's husband Subhash Kumar refused to conduct the last rites till the two accused were arrested. Finally when the Chief Minister stepped in and dismissed the the three senior policemen, Sarita was cremated. Dalal said a government job would be given to Subhash to help him raise his two minor daughters.

Addressing a separate press conference, Haryana Chief Secretary Dharamvir said that in future, responsibility would be fixed in cases of sexual harrasment where action is delayed. He added that the state Government had decided to set up a "web-based system" so that people could register their complaints over the Internet from anywhere.

Five teams are hunting for Balraj and Silk Ram in Haryana and Rajasthan. "After arresting them, we will quickly put their case in court and make effort that it is tried in a fast-track court," Dalal said. Additional Director General of Police (Crime) Sharat Kumar is reaching Rohtak tomorrow to investigate why action against the two accused cops was delayed and fix responsibility.

Additional DGP V B Singh, in whose office Sarita died, confirmed to The Indian Express: "To my knowledge, the Rohtak police did not get Sarita medically examined, neither when she lodged the first complaint, nor even after registration of the criminal case."

Meanwhile, it has emerged that Sarita wrote two suicide notes. While she carried one to the ADGP's office in Panchkula, she left the other at home. It is only in the note found at home that she seems to have written "now my husband is also leaving me", which has been scratched out. Subhash denies that he tried to scratch the words out, saying he can't read.

He adds that he only realised Sarita's intentions when he got somebody to read the note, and that he immediately asked his father-in-law to leave for Panchkula. Moments after that, he says, he got a call from a DSP telling him that Sarita had consumed poison.

Heading: PM pitches for deal: No US pressure, it will open windows to Russia, France - Indian Express
Content:
Paying tributes to the late Rajesh Pilot, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh recounted the pioneering role played by him in laying the foundation for rural telephony. He was speaking at a function after releasing a postage stamp to commemorate the eighth death anniversary of Pilot at Balayogi Auditorium at the parliament House.

Pilot, a popular leader from the Gurjjar community, was killed in a road accident in his Lok Sabha constituency, Dausa, in 2000. It may be a coincidence, but there is no denying the fact that the Congress-led UPA Government has chosen to invoke Pilot's memory when the Gujar community, demanding its inclusion in the Scheduled Tribe category, is up in arms against the BJP Government in Rajasthan. Ever since Pilot's death, the Congress has not been able to prop up a Gurjjar leader who comes anywhere near him in terms of popular appeal in the community.

Congress president Sonia Gandhi was the guest of honour at the function. Pilot's widow Rama Pilot sat on the podium next to Gandhi, while her MP-son Sachin Pilot presented bouquets welcoming both the Prime Minister and the Congress chief. Communications Minister A Raja was the special guest at the function.

Speaking extempore in Hindi, Manmohan Singh recalled his association with Pilot in the Union Cabinet as well as the Congress Working Committee and said he gave a "new direction" to every department which he handled. He made "relentless efforts" for the spread of rural telephony during its formative years. Had he been alive, the massive strides made by his Government in the development of rural roads would have made him proud.

According to the Prime Minister, as interior minister Pilot made tremendous efforts to improve the situation in Jammu and Kashmir. He also took an initiative to solve the Bodo problem in Assam. As Singh talked of Pilot's role, value system and contribution in public life, he made a faux pas too by repeatedly referring to "Rajivji" instead of "Rajesh Pilotji."

Jagat Singh, a childhood friend of Pilot, proposed a vote of thanks. The gathering cheered as a nervous Jagat Singh, a villager, stretched his hand towards Sonia Gandhi while greeting her after making a speech. However, Gandhi graciously responded and shook hands with him, much to the delight of photographers.

Heading: Rising on a Tawang peak overlooking Tibet: 80-ft statue of the female Buddha - Indian Express
Content:
A week before the crucial UPA-Left meeting on June 18, government efforts to push through the Indo-US nuclear deal gained fresh momentum with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh making it clear that "domestic politics" was stalling the deal which had no strings attached to it.

"There is no pressure from US to sign the NPT or any other international arrangement," Singh told Indian Foreign Service probationers today. The deal also came up for discussion at a 30-minute meeting he had with US Ambassador David Mulford.

Pitching for the deal while addressing the probationers, Singh said it would "end nuclear apartheid" and "open up new possibilities of cooperation, not only with the US but all other nuclear powers like Russia and France".

Later in the day, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee said "nuclear energy is an option and we shall have to go (for it)." Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a book launch, he said the UPA-Left meeting to sort out differences on the deal was scheduled for June 18 and "we will have to wait till then".

"Given the oil price scenario, we seriously need to consider how our energy basket may be expanded so as to meet the deficit in India's energy requirement," Mukherjee said.

The PM, meanwhile, told the probationers: "I think it is for the first time we got the US to appreciate that India is a nuclear weapons state, that India has the right to develop nuclear power to protect its strategic interests, and that it is a decision that must be made by the people of India not subject to any international supervision or any international interference."

"And despite the fact that we are not a signatory to the NPT, and we have also said that if the CTBT came into being we will not sign it, there is no pressure from the US on India to sign the NPT or any other international arrangement of that sort to enter into nuclear cooperation for civil energy."

Singh's assertion comes at a time when the Left parties as well as the BJP are raising concerns that there is US pressure to sign the nuclear deal.

"It (the deal) has run into some difficulties, but it protects our national interest, it protects our capacity to use the nuclear power to protect our strategic interests. At the same time it opens us new opportunities for civilian cooperation and without that, I think, the trade in dual technologies — sensitive advanced technologies — cannot become a reality. But our domestic politics has prevented us from going ahead; I still continue to hope that we will make progress in the months that lie ahead. But it is very important for us to move forward to end this nuclear apartheid that the world has sought to impose on India," he said.

Mulford's meeting with PM took place in connection with the upcoming G-8 Summit in Hokkaido next month. Given that Singh will meet US President George W Bush at the summit, sources said, Mulford broadly outlined the issues that could be discussed at the meeting.

The nuclear deal would figure in these talks with Mulford conveying that Washington hoped India would be able to resolve domestic issues and take the next steps. Sources said this was a preparatory meeting ahead of the summit and a whole set of issues, including rising oil and food prices, were touched upon.

The Prime Minister, in his address to the probationers, also shared the "growing fear" that "security of nations can be threatened by nuclear weapons and sensitive technologies falling into the hands of terrorist elements," adding that "terrorism today is an international phenomenon, that there are still states who are sometimes actively backing the terrorist elements, and that there is a growing importance of the non-state actors in areas relating to terror."

Stressing the need for a "peaceful neighbourhood", he referred to the border dispute with China: "We have in the last four years actively engaged through our special representatives to find pragmatic pathways to handle this complicated issue. Some progress is being made but I think there is a long, arduous journey ahead of us."

Heading: BJP top brass debated fallout, nuanced its oppn - Indian Express
Content:
At the centre of a boundary dispute between India and China, Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh is now gearing for the installation of a 80-feet high statue of Tara — the female Buddha, typically associated with Buddhist tantra practice as preserved in Tibetan Buddhism, is also the "mother of liberation" — atop a strategically located peak which is 11,000 feet high and overlooks Tibet and Bhutan.

With infrastructure upgrade in Tawang already high on the government's agenda — several projects, including an airstrip on a hilltop, are being expedited — this move to install a statue is being viewed as another assertion of Indian control over the area. The Centre has already released seed-money for the project, estimated to cost US $2.33 million.

Officially christened as the White Tara Project (WTP), the project envisages developing the Lumla peak into a Buddhist tourist destination, complete with prayer halls, meditation centres, museum and a library. The giant statue of Tara Devi is intended to give the spot a distinct tourist identity in addition to attracting Tibetan Buddhists among whom the deity enjoys a special place.

Work for construction of a 18-feet high Dolma Lhakhang (abode at the base of the structure) is on at the hill site. "This structure will form the base of the statue. Work on setting up the White Tara statue on a 1,000 petalled lotus will begin shortly.There will also be a museum, Stupa, car park, bazaar, eatery, hostel and landscaping," said sources linked to the project.

"The location of the peak is its greatest advantage. One can see Bhutan from one side and Tibet from the other. We plan to develop it as a religious-cum-tourist destination and attract Buddhists from Tibet, Bhutan in addition to Indian tourists," Lumla MLA T G Rinpoche, project prime mover, told The Indian Express.

Heading: Marksheets in hand, MPs, MLAs line up for Rahul’s Talent Search - Indian Express
Content:
Aware there was a big disconnect between the party's stated position on the Indo-US nuclear deal and its middle class constituency, the BJP has effected a subtle shift in its stand, making itself appear more receptive to the idea "without ceding the nationalist space".

At a BJP core group meeting about a month ago, it was senior leader M Venkaiah Naidu who said that the party's position on the deal "was not going down well with its core constituency of middle class". "Naidu implied that the BJP must not get overzealous like the Left in opposing the deal," said a top source.

Party president Rajnath Singh and its deputy leader in Lok Sabha V K Malhotra saw merit in the argument. Party general secretary Arun Jaitley felt that the party's position needed to be more "nuanced". Senior leader Sushma Swaraj said the terms of reference of the nuclear debate in India were not the same as in the US (and "hence must be opposed"). All the leaders, however, said that India could not give up the right to conduct future nuclear tests.

The party's 11-member core group has Atal Bihari Vajpayee, L K Advani, Rajnath Singh, Jaswant Singh, Murli Manohar Joshi, Venkaiah Naidu, Arun Jaitley, Sushma Swaraj, Ram Lal, Bal Apte and V K Malhotra as members.

"We felt that we have come a little too far in our opposition (to the deal). Yet we couldn't have jettisoned the position formulated on the issue. Summing up the debate, Advani said that India cannot accept a ban on further nuclear tests but the party was okay with other provisions of the deal," said a leader present at the meeting.

Speaking at a function in Pune last week, Advani said that "the party would not accept a ban on Pokhran-III" as it would compromise India's position as a nuclear power. "Remove this ban in the agreement by renegotiating the deal and we will not have any objection," he said. He had taken more or less the same line at an ASSOCHAM function on June 2: "We do not basically oppose the nuclear agreement... Our reservation is only on the written word that there should not be any further nuclear tests..."

Responding to the PM's observations today that "our domestic politics have prevented us from going ahead with the nuclear deal", Venkaiah Naidu said "the government should have evolved political consensus before going ahead with it".

"It is the Prime Minister and his party that is to be blamed for the present state of the nuclear deal. Although he is blaming the Opposition for the failure of the deal, his supposition is about the Left parties," Naidu said.

The BJP had earlier stuck to the line that the "the deal is not acceptable in its present form".

Former president A P J Abdul Kalam's recent go-ahead for the deal too has had an effect on the BJP top brass. A senior leader, also present at the core group meeting, said after Kalam's observations: "Are we bigger patriots then Kalam? Can we question his credentials on science and technology?"

Heading: A child labourer’s dream, an award-winning movie - Indian Express
Content:
Last Thursday about 30-odd young men and women from Madhya Pradesh anxiously awaited their turn at 12, Tughlaq Lane, New Delhi, for an interview that would shape their future careers. Among them were Khargone MP Arun Yadav, Khilchipur MLA Priyavrat Singh and Bahoriband MLA Nisith Patel. In their hands they clutched their Class X and XII marksheets.

The man who would interview them was AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi, who is in the middle of a country-wide Talent Search programme to reshape the Congress ahead of the polls. The process has already led to selection of "aam admi ke sipahi" (common man's soldiers), to carry the Government's message and achievements to villages.

Thursday's interview was part of another process: to purge the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) of "over-aged" leaders. Among the mandatory conditions for interviewees was producing their original marksheets as proof of their age. As per the party's constitution for Youth Congress members, they can't be above 35 years.

Rahul started calling the candidates in one by one. The questions were simple; the answers perhaps not: How is the Congress doing in Madhya Pradesh? What about the Indian Youth Congress (IYC)? What do you suggest to strengthen these organisations? How are the UPA Government's schemes being implemented? What are the burning issues in the state? What do you suggest the party should do to win the ensuing elections, etc?

The interviews lasted 5-10 minutes each.

It was the penultimate round of the Talent Search programme, launched by Rahul after his appointment as AICC general secretary in charge of the Youth Congress.

A panel of party leaders — including Anand Sharma, P R Dasmunshi, B K Hari Prasad, V Narayansamy, Jitin Prasada, Sachin Pilot, Sandeep Dikshit, and incumbent IYC president Ashok Tanwar, among others — had earlier scouted around in different states to shortlist the candidates from among the NSUI and IYC through interviews.

Thursday's interview at Rahul's official residence involved candidates shortlisted by this panel in Madhya Pradesh. Fourteen of them made it to the final round the next day, Friday.

This involved Rahul holding one-on-one interactions, lasting 10-15 minutes, with each of them separately. The entire group was then split into two for a group discussion. The final interviews and discussion involved similar sets of questions.

"It was like an interview in the corporate world. I was told Rahulji was giving us marks in terms of organisational ability, communication skill, ideological commitment, values, political understanding, etc. Although nobody was to be rejected, everybody was to be given assignment as per their area of interest and ability," one of the participants told The Indian Express.

Although the results were not declared immediately, Rahul made it known that one of them would go on to become president of the Youth Congress in Madhya Pradesh — a post lying vacant for around four years — while others would be accommodated as per their skill and understanding.

The Talent Search exercise has been completed in about a dozen states. As a result, three IYC state presidents have been changed so far, with Pijush Hazarika being appointed Assam Youth Congress chief on Tuesday. IYC presidents of Karnataka and Delhi were changed earlier.

According to IYC sources, Rahul intends to change all state presidents and put in their place those he selects through the Talent Search programme. No wonder, MLAs and MPs are also turning up in the queue.

Khilchipur MLA Priyavrat Singh, 30, told The Indian Express on phone: "Now that Rahulji himself is taking so much interest in strengthening the organisation, it has come as a great inspiration to us. I wanted to be a part of his mission."

Bahoriband MLA Nishith Patel was equally inspired by "Rahulji's commitment".

Rahul's emphasis on the age criterion could come as a big blow to many IYC leaders. Himachal Pradesh Youth Congress president Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, for instance, is over 40 years' old and has been occupying the post for the past nine years. Youth Congress presidents of West Bengal, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Punjab and Jammu & Kashmir are also above the age limit.

"Rahulji has made it quite clear that there would be no compromise on age limit," says IYC president Ashok Tanwar.

The "finds" of the Talent Search programme have been deployed as "aam admi ke sipahi". Under this programme, Rahul has appointed two coordinators for each state, who will select two coordinators for each district. The district coordinators will select block coordinators who, in turn, will select two coordinators in each panchayat.

The aam admi ke sipahi will assigned to do "social audits" of all Central schemes, especially the NREGA, pensions, scholarships etc, ensure that these schemes reach the people, and hold agitations for their proper implementation.

The "army" would initially be deployed in 300-350 districts — particularly all districts in the poll-bound states.

Heading: China revokes 700 toy export licences: report - Indian Express
Content:
Priyanandanan dropped out of school when he was in Class VII. His father had fallen ill and his mother's job as a manual labourer was not enough to feed the family of five—he was the eldest and he had two younger sisters. At age 12, he began working in a small factory making tea cups in his village, Vallachira, earning Rs 2.5 a day. Then, he moved on to become assistant to the village goldsmith.

The child labourer who made the country's best feature film of 2006 is worried by all the adulation. "My films are intensely cathartic to me and I doubt if they will ever make money. But I can't negate myself and do some crass commercial film for my family's sake... and after the publicity, I can no longer expect people to give me a manual job in my village anymore, either," says Priyanandanan, 42, whose Pulijanmam won the national award announced on Tuesday.

The son of a poor village sculptor of wooden elephants ("Elephants were all that my father sculpted, all his life"), Priyanandanan discovered theatre early. "My heart was always in theatre, and I used to beg for small roles in plays staged in the village during festivals, then moved on to bigger roles. The more I came to know plays, the more I knew that there was a whole lot more to it than commercial nonsense. I started seriously reading up everything on theatre that I could get in the libraries, went around meeting the big playwrights and directors in Kerala and finally began directing plays on my own," he says.

While the small bands of serious theatre lovers applauded, he was jobless and running up huge debts—even his tiny village home was attached.

Films were a natural progression. For seven years, Priyanandanan struggled under some of Kerala's eminent parallel film makers, until he picked up the courage to try out his maiden film, Neythukaran (The weaver), running from one producer to another and being shown the door. Neythukaran fetched three awards, including the national award for best actor.

As Kerala toasted Priyanandanan, few knew what he had been through to make that movie even after it got off the block : "Producers walked out half way, actors, technicians and everyone else had to forgo their charges—friends had to beg and borrow to rent theatres for a single screening, because no one wanted a non-commercial movie."

Even after Neythukaran fetched rave reviews, Priyanandanan kept trudging all over for months for someone to produce Pulijanmam. "I was told, advised, even sneered at for lugging a script and a concept that would never make money. Until a producer, M G Vijay, told me to go ahead."

Priyanandanan is unfazed that not many people would be seeing his national award-winning movie. "I would be more than happy if at least one movie house in one district each shows it just once a day. I would be content if it is watched by a few people who know and believe in the strength and potential of movies," he says.

He is already doing the spadework for his next movie, based on a popular Malayalam literary work, Yakshi. He expects that too to be no cakewalk, especially after even the Kerala government's promised subsidy of Rs 4 lakh for his Pulijanmam has somehow got stuck.

Heading: Obama’s choice of insider draws fire - Indian Express
Content:
Beijing has revoked the export licences of 700 toy factories over safety failings, state media reported on Wednesday, after a series of high-profile scandals hit the image of Chinese goods overseas.

Beijing launched a massive campaign to inspect all 3,540 toy firms with export permits last August after tens of millions of Chinese-made toys were recalled globally due to design or manufacturing flaws.

It barred 700 firms — nearly one in five — from exporting because they failed to meet safety standards, the China Daily quoted a senior safety official as saying.

"After the inspection, the overall situation regarding the production of toys for export has been greatly improved," said Li Changjiang, head of the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine. Li made the comments after meeting Meglena Kuneva, the visiting EU commissioner for consumer policy.

Kuneva's visit was her third since last July, when a spate of quality scandals surrounding Chinese exports ranging from seafood to toys added new tensions to trade relations with Europe and the United States.

China exported around 22 billion toys globally every year, a quarter of which went to Europe, the China Daily said. The EU will continue to watch its imports closely, monitoring for shoddy products and toys, with high chemical content and dangerous small parts considered the major problems, the paper added.

Heading: Conservatives train guns on Michelle: ‘Obama’s bitter half’ - Indian Express
Content:
Last month, Senator Barack Obama turned to James A Johnson, a former Fannie Mae chief executive and Washington insider since the Carter administration, to lead the vetting of potential running mates for the Democratic Party's presumptive presidential nominee.

But four years earlier, as Johnson was angling for a job if Senator John F Kerry was elected president, Fannie Mae did some vetting of its own. Company executives had grown so worried about the lucrative consulting deal they had cut with their former CEO that they considered enlisting an outside investigator to comb through the deal "in light of issues that could come up during Senate confirmation . . . or White House review of the consulting contract," according to company documents unearthed by federal regulators.

For Republicans seeking to tarnish Obama's image as a squeaky-clean outsider hoping to clean up Washington — not to mention divert attention from questions about lobbyists working in Senator John McCain's campaign — Obama's embrace of Johnson has been a gift.

"He's tagged himself as a different kind of politician," said Republican strategist Mark Corallo. "He's supposed to transcend party, transcend politics. He's exploited that more than anyone in recent memory, and it becomes demoralising to all the starry-eyed Obamaphiles who are saying, 'I thought he was different.'"

The questions about Johnson began after the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday that he received more than $2 million in home loans that might have been below average market rates from Countrywide Financial, a partner of Fannie Mae and a leading purveyor of the kind of subprime mortgages that spawned a national housing crisis.

Responding to questions yesterday about that article, Obama said: "I am not vetting my VP search committee for their mortgages. These aren't folks who are working for me. They're not people who I have assigned to a particular job in a future administration."

But the questions surrounding Johnson's past suggest the difficulties Obama will face as his campaign expands from an underdog insurgency to a general-election operation. He has little choice but to pick up experienced political insiders — and the baggage they bring with them.

"This is a game that can be played," Obama told reporters in St Louis. "Everybody who is tangentially related to our campaign, I think, is going to have a whole host of relationships. I would have to hire the vetter to vet the vetters."

As CEO of Fannie Mae, Johnson, a former chief of staff to Vice President Walter F Mondale and chairman of the board of the Kennedy Center, was the beneficiary of accounting in which Fannie Mae's earnings were manipulated so that executives could earn larger bonuses. The accounting manipulation for 1998 resulted in the maximum payouts to Fannie Mae's senior executives — $1.9 million in Johnson's case — when the company's performance that year would have otherwise resulted in no bonuses at all, according to reports in 2004 and 2006 by the Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight.

Heading: Sudan investigates plane crash, toll unclear - Indian Express
Content:
They loved to hate Hillary Rodham Clinton. They loved to hate Teresa Heinz Kerry. And now, it appears, conservative voices are energetically taking on Michelle Obama.

"Mrs Grievance" bellowed the cover of a recent National Review in reference to her. The magazine's online edition titled an essay about her stump speech "America's Unhappiest Millionaire".

Michelle Malkin, the popular conservative blogger, called her "Obama's bitter half."

Even the relatively liberal online magazine Slate piled on. In a piece subtitled "Is Michelle Obama responsible for the Jeremiah Wright fiasco?" the contrarian Christopher Hitchens blamed her for her husband's pastor troubles since she was a member of the church first.

The would-be first lady does not make pronouncements about policy and has insisted her priority in the White House would be her two young daughters. But Michelle Obama has an earthy sense of humour that sometimes gets her in trouble. And in speeches, she shares her belief that the country's spirit is broken and in need of repair — by her husband, Illinois Senator Barack Obama, whom she often describes as "special".

It was an unscripted remark as she spoke in February about the enthusiastic response to his message of hope that set off conservatives: "And let me tell you something," she told a Wisconsin crowd. "For the first time in my adult lifetime, I am really proud of my country."

The Obama campaign clarified her remarks right away: "What she meant is that she's really proud at this moment because for the first time in a long time, thousands of Americans who've never participated in politics before are coming out in record numbers to build a grassroots movement for change."

But conservatives pressed the attack. John Podhoretz, editor of Commentary, wrote that she'd inadvertently revealed "the pseudo-messianic nature of the Obama candidacy".

The issue has shown no signs of going away.

In what could be seen as a test run for future attacks, the Tennessee Republican Party last month posted a Web video crosscutting her gaffe with declarations from average folks about how they've always been proud of their country.

Bill Hobbs, spokesman for the Tennessee GOP, said the party was stunned and delighted by national publicity garnered by the cheaply made video, which coincided with a fundraising visit to the state by Michelle Obama. "Our goal was to get the local media to play that clip of what she said back in February," Hobbs said. "The amazing thing was this thing blew up nationally before any local media even covered it."

Heading: 700-pound Mexican man hopes to stand for wedding - Indian Express
Content:
Sudanese investigators on Wednesday were trying to determine what caused a jetliner that had just landed in a thunderstorm to veer off a runway and burst into flames in Sudan's capital.

At least 29 people were killed inside the burning plane, while 171 managed to escape, said Sudan Civil Aviation Authority spokesman Abdel Hafez Abdel Rahim Mahmoud said, adding that 14 still remained unaccounted for. Many passengers fleeing the burning plane did bother to pass through customs, making the toll initially difficult to ascertain.

By Wednesday morning, the fire has been completely extinguished and civil defence officials were now examining the wreckage to determine the causes of the crash, police spokesman Maj Gen Mohammed Abdel Majid al-Tayeb told the official SUNA news agency.

The Sudan Airways jetliner appeared to have gone off the runway after landing at Khartoum International Airport, and several loud explosions resounded as fire raced through the aircraft, an Associated Press reporter at the scene said.

The roaring blaze dwarfed the Airbus A310's shattered fuselage as firefighters sprayed water, Sudanese TV footage showed. Ambulances and firetrucks rushed to the scene, and media were kept away.

One survivour said the landing was "rough", and there was a sharp impact several minutes later.

"The right wing was on fire," said the passenger, who did not give his name. He said smoke got into the cockpit and some people started opening the emergency exits. Soon, fire engulfed the plane, he told Sudanese television.

Heading: Makeover for cartoon characters to match 21st century - Indian Express
Content:
Manuel Uribe, who once weighed a half ton but has slimmed down to about 700 pounds, celebrates his 43rd birthday on Wednesday with a simple wish for the coming year: to be able to stand on his own two feet to get married.

Interviewed at his home in northern Mexico, where he can still do little more than sit up on a bed, Uribe said more than two years of steady dieting have helped him drop about 550 pounds from his Guinness record weight of 1,235 pounds.

He hopes Guinness representatives will confirm in July that he holds a second title: The world's greatest loser of weight.

But Uribe is still unable to walk his fiancee, Claudia Solis, down the aisle.

"It frustrates me a little, because it is not easy to get out," said Uribe, who has not been able to leave bed for the last six years.

His most recent attempt to escape the house — to attend Solis' 38th birthday party in March— fell through when a flatbed tow truck brought to transport his reinforced bed got caught beneath an underpass.

But Uribe vowed not to be deterred: "We are in love, and this year my birthday wish is to be able to stand when we get married," he said.

Uribe said he met Solis, a 38-year-old hairdresser, four years ago. They have been together for the last two.

"We are a couple," Uribe said. "We have sex, and in the eyes of God we are already married."

Proudly showing off her sparkling engagement ring, Solis said life with a heavyweight is not always easy.

"I bathe him every day, and we get along very well," she said. "At times, yes, people say things ... that it's a fake relationship, but what we have is real."

Solis said her family initially opposed the match with Uribe, because her first husband, who was also obese, died of respiratory failure.

"They were worried about me being involved with another fat man, because they thought another husband would die on me," she said.

Uribe, a former auto parts dealer, said his birthday party Wednesday will be a low-key dinner with the family.

"We were going to go out, but the last time out scared me so much," he said. "When we crashed into the lighting conduits on the underpass, I thought we were going to get an electric shock."

Heading: King exits, says no role in palace massacre - Indian Express
Content:
Strawberry Shortcake was having an identity crisis. The "it" doll and cartoon star of the 1980s was just not connecting with modern girls. Too candy-obsessed. Too ditzy. Too fond of wearing bloomers.

So her owner, American Greetings Properties, worked for a year on what it calls a "fruit-forward" makeover.

Strawberry Shortcake, part of a line of scented dolls, now prefers fresh fruit to gumdrops, appears to wear just a dab of lipstick (but no rouge), and spends her time chatting on a cellphone instead of brushing her calico cat, Custard. Her new look was unveiled Tuesday, along with plans for a new line of toys from Hasbro.

She is not the only aging fictional star to get a facelift. An unusually large number of classic characters for children are being freshened up and reintroduced— on store shelves, on the Internet and on television screen— as their corporate owners try to cater to parents' nostalgia and children's YouTube-era sensibilities. Adding momentum is a retail sector hoping to find refuge from a rough economy in the tried and true.

Warner Brothers hopes to "reinvigorate and reimagine" Bugs Bunny and Scooby-Doo through a new virtual world on the Internet, where people will be able to dress up the characters pretty much any way they want. American Greetings is dusting off another of its lines, the Care Bears, which will return with a fresh look this fall (less belly fat, longer eyelashes). And 4Kids Entertainment, which licenses the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, will revive them next year in new video games, where they will have more muscles and less attitude.

Even Mickey Mouse is getting an update, although the Walt Disney Company is still mulling what tweaks to make.
