Heading: Army ops, surrenders bring ULFA down to 400 men - Indian Express
Content:
Jharkhand's Palamau district administration, in its first official report on the May 15 murder of social activist Lalit Mehta, has rejected claims by NGOs and social activists that the killing was linked to an audit by Mehta which had detected irregularities in works under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme in the district.

Maintaining there was "no substance" in the allegations being made by activists, Palamau DC Nagendra Prasad Singh and SP Deepak Kumar Verma, in their report dated May 31, have in fact slammed development economist-activist Jean Dreze — he is also member, Central Employment Guarantee Council — for orchestrating, what they alleged, was a campaign to malign the district administration.

Dreze was unavailable for comment on Thursday.

The report, referring to statements by Mehta's brothers and wife, suggests that the murder motive may have been linked to money as "Lalit Mehta played an important role in large sums of monetary transactions" involving the Vikas Sahyog Kendra, the NGO he founded.

The report accuses Dreze and his team of social auditors of "creating an environment to paint the Palamau administration, along with the Jharkhand government, as deeply entrenched in corruption and suggesting that works under NREG in all districts of Jharkhand, Palamau included, is being done only on paper."

Referring to the Mehta murder probe by ASP Sandeep Kadam Basant, the report says the probe team questioned Dreze and his other associates at Vikas Sahyog Kendra in Chhattarpur and were told that one Iqbal Hussain was an eyewitness to the incident.

According to the report, when Hussain was traced and questioned, he told police he was in the area where Mehta's body was found on May 15. Hussain is quoted as saying he saw 5-6 men on motorcycles around 3.15 pm. On one motorcycle, there were three men and the hand of the man sitting in the middle was dangling. The men parked the motorcycles, went into the fields and returned after 15-20 minutes. The report says Hussain identified one of the men as Alimuddin.

But the police point out that while Hussain claims having seen the men at 3.15 pm, Mehta's body had been sent for post-mortem to Daltonganj at 3.45 pm. According to the report, police learnt that Hussain named Alimuddin because he had "old enmity" with him and both had even been in jail at the same time in separate cases.

Police investigations could not establish Alimuddin's link to the Mehta case and he was let off on a bond, says the report.

Recalling the sequence of events, the report in fact mentions Mehta was "last seen with Dreze". Also referring to an audit by Dreze and his team which alleged "irregularity" and "corruption" by two officials in the same block, the report says the charges against the officials were "without substance".

The report alleges that Dreze and his team "took advantage of semi-literate tribal workers" and got them to "sign on a complaint" that the two officials had taken bribe money of Rs 4,500 in two instalments.

After Dreze submitted the complaint, an inquiry was conducted but the complainants, in the presence of a magistrate, stated that they had received appropriate wages and because they were semi-literate, Dreze and his team got them to sign on a paper, the report states.

Heading: Post-Bora, CM looks to Sonia for pep talk - Indian Express
Content:
A series of encounters and an unprecedented number of surrenders over the past 12 months has brought down the number of armed ULFA cadres to just over 400 from an estimated strength of 1,000 two years ago, show latest intelligence estimates.

While a concerted Army offensive since the start of this year has pushed up casualty figures to over 64 armed cadres, intelligence officials say the biggest dent for the ULFA has come from a deluge of surrenders that are taking place due to a 'loss of ideology' within the organisation.

The latest estimate, drawn up from reports by several intelligence agencies, reveals that of the over 400 armed and active ULFA cadres, a majority have taken temporary shelter in the adjoining states of Meghalaya, Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh in the wake of recent intensified Army operations.

Barely two years ago, the number of active ULFA cadres was believed to be close to 1,000, with most of them believed to be operational within the state. The intelligence estimate also says that ULFA is finding it extremely hard to recruit new cadres into the organisation.

Adding to this is the large number of surrenders that has rocked the armed group over the past year. The Army insists that a new policy of bringing forward families of ULFA cadres to appeal for peace is paying dividends.

In the month of October last year, over 60 ultras laid down their arms during a sustained surrender drive. Sources say the series of surrenders completely undermined the dreaded 28 ULFA Battalion that was active in upper Assam besides weakening the 709, 109 and 27 battalions.

"The ULFA has become a rag tag extortion force due to a complete loss of ideology. While the top leadership is leading a luxurious life in Bangladesh, the junior leadership operational within the country has given up on the ideology," said an intelligence officer.

However, the armed group continues to find a safe haven in Bangladesh where its top leadership is established. Officials from the security establishment say while Myanmar has been launching operations against Indian insurgent groups, Bangladesh authorities are still reluctant to crack down on terror camps along the border.

Heading: Assam, Meghalaya set up panel to look into border dispute - Indian Express
Content:
Congress president Sonia Gandhi's visit here on Friday could prove to be the much-needed morale booster Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi was looking forward to, following the arrest of sacked state education minister Ripun Bora by the CBI on corruption charges.

Sonia will address a kisan rally of the party and give away the Srimanta Sankaradeva Award, instituted in 1986 after the 16th century Assamese saint-reformer, during her day-long visit to the state capital.

The visit comes at a time when the image of the Congress party has suffered a heavy blow following Bora's arrest from a guesthouse in New Delhi on June 3. He was trying to bribe a CBI officer with Rs 10 lakh to get his name removed from the inquiry into the murder of political rival Daniel Topno in his hometown Gohpur in 2000.

Chief Minister Gogoi has now asked his party workers, including MLAs and ministers to go all out in countering the Opposition's attack on the party over the Bora case.

Gogoi has also ordered a high-level inquiry into alleged corruption and anomalies in the construction of a flood-protection structure at Matmora in Upper Assam. Additional chief secretary P P Varma has been asked to probe the charges against Flood Control and Water Resources Minister Bharat Chandra Narah.

The Opposition has described the Congress-led Government headed by Gogoi as having failed on all fronts and accused the Chief Minister of protecting several corrupt ministers with criminal cases against them. Those whom the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) and BJP have accused of having such records include Excise Minister Gautam Roy and Narah.

Heading: Rao back at helm, revamps TRS panel, fires dist units - Indian Express
Content:
Assam and Meghalaya have set up a coordination committee to look into the border dispute between the two states. This decision was taken after an hour-long meeting between Assam Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi and his Meghalaya counterpart Donkupar Roy here on Wednesday.

An official spokesman here said the coordination committee will comprise chief secretaries and revenue secretaries of both states, apart from deputy commissioners of Kamrup district and West Khasi Hills district. Survey of India officials would be asked to assist in resolving the disputes, the spokesman added.

The committee will examine the disputes in the Langpih area and submit its report to both the Governments within six months. The same committee would also look into the border disputes between the two states in other districts.

Assam and Meghalaya were headed for a major controversy after the former set up a health centre at Langpih village in Kamrup district earlier this month. Meghalaya claimed the village belonged to it and was being encroached upon by Assam. Both the states also agreed to maintain status quo in the Langpih area.

Heading: For terminal rabies patients, this Madurai hospital makes it worse - Indian Express
Content:
Sending out a clear message to the rival factions, TRS chief K Chandrasekhara Rao said on Thursday that his party would contest all the seats in Telangana in the 2009 Assembly elections.

A fortnight after the party's debacle in the byelections, KCR, who is back at the helm of the party's affairs, disbanded the TRS's 150-member executive committee, fired all the party's district units and asked several local-level leaders to quit if they did not see any future in the party.

It is being seen as a shrewd move by KCR to scuttle any attempts by the rival faction to take over the leadership of the party. After the party won only seven seats and lost nine in the byelections, the rival factions in the TRS became more powerful as they had 11 MLAs. In fact, fearing that the rival faction would take over the main TRS, the executive committee put tremendous pressure on KCR to withdraw his resignation and take charge of the party afresh. KCR, who resigned on June 1, relented under pressure from the same executive committee that he disbanded on Thursday. He is learnt to have taken the step to quell resentment and further rebellion. He also dissolved the district units, which, he felt, failed to gauge the mood of the people before the elections, resulting in the party's losses. KCR said a small-sized new executive would be constituted on June 20.

In his first major meeting with the party after he withdrew his resignation, he decided to shift the blame on other party leaders, accusing them of being responsible for the TRS's poor performance. "If you think this party has no future, you can go," he told TRS leaders at a party meeting where he took command again as its chief.

KCR also announced that a policymaking committee, which would include outsiders or non-party members, would be constituted to advise the TRS on framing policies and strategies.

The TRS chief warned that the party would now take up militant programmes like organising bandhs, rasta roko and demonstrations on certain issues like Telangana statehood and inflation.

If KCR is on a sticky wicket after the party's losses, he did not show it as he took charge of the party affairs again. In defiance, he announced that the TRS would independently contest all the seats in the next general Assembly elections in Telangana. "We will announce the names of candidates before any other party. There is no question of tying up with anyone this time. We will contest all the seats independently. A panel of four or five candidates would be short-listed in each constituency. Based on the chances of winning, a final candidate would be chosen. There would be equal representation of candidates from all backgrounds," he said.

Political observers feel that the TRS wants to send out a message that it might have lost some seats in the byelections, but it is not finished yet and is preparing to come back with a bang in the next elections. KCR is sending out feelers to TRS rebels who covertly support the Congress. He is also trying to placate his nephew and MLA T Harish Rao, who is apparently disappointed with KCR's leadership and blames him for the party's poor performance in the bypolls. Party sources said, KCR is willing to give him more responsibilities and a senior position in the party to keep him under his control and prevent a possible rebellions.

Heading: He fought for his dead son for 20 yrs, but wasn’t alive when justice came - Indian Express
Content:
Far away from the swanky corporate hospitals in Chennai that make Tamil Nadu a global healthcare destination, a rabies-infected girl had a tragic death, locked up in an isolation cell of a Government hospital that has more things in common to a kennel than a hospital ward.

Thirteen-year-old Kavita's painful death on Wednesday was not made any easy by the cell, a small room with metal bars and padlock that is used to confine rabies patients and persons suffering from mental ailments. The Class VI student from Sivaganga district was the second person to die inside the cell this month alone—15-year-old Shivakumar of Sivakasi had an equally tragic death earlier this month. It was also the fourth death due to rabies reported in the 166-year-old Government Rajaji Hospital (GRH), Madurai, in the past two months.

The cell, doctors said, was the only way to keep the rabies patient in complete isolation, even from relatives, as the chance of contracting the disease is very high. "The bite injuries were on the head and hastened the death. The anti-rabies vaccine takes about 4-7 days to act, but in this case, that delay was enough for the disease to go beyond control," said hospital dean S M Sivakumar. He said the hospital's effort was to isolate rabies patients from everyone else considering the threat of disease contraction. According to sources, though technology has progressed by leaps and bounds there was a lack of expertise in handling such cases. Local residents claimed rabies cases were mostly attended by the paramedical staff as most doctors don't want to take a chance for a lost cause. After the public complained about the tardy facilities at the GRH, the CPI-M had conducted a signature campaign urging the state Government to maintain the hospital in a better manner.

On Thursday, the authorities were trying their best to present a good picture—the cell was being cleaned and white-washed. Sivakumar said he would write to the Government to repair the cell. Health Minister M R K Panneerselvam said the Dean did not need his permission to undertake maintenance work, but added that officials will be asked to look into the matter. "Such patients undergo a painful death and are put in isolation cells for the sake of others' safety. I will ask officials to check the matter immediately so that the conditions are improved," said the minister.

Meanwhile, R Alagumani, an advocate of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court has decided to move a PIL urging the court to look into treatment of rabies patients at the hospital.

Heading: Karnataka Govt withdraws its temple circular - Indian Express
Content:
It was a father's battle for justice for 20 long years. But when the law finally caught up with the perpetrators he was not there to witness it.

For 11 years Thankappan, a daily labourer, had preserved his son's body soaked in formalin (a disinfectant and preservative) in a concrete tank he had especially built for the purpose after Gopi, 21, died mysteriously in police custody in 1988 in a Kerala village.

Although the police had claimed Gopi had committed suicide by stabbing himself with a fluorescent tube, the distraught father refused to believe it and vowed not to cremate his son's body until justice was done. Thankappan had to wait for 11 years before the Kerala High Court order an inquiry into the role of the then circle inspector of Cherthala police station Srikanadan Nair and Sub-Inspector Prabhakaran. It was then, in 1999, that the old man cremated Gopi's body.

After 20 years, the Chief Judicial Magistrate's court found Nair and Prabhakaran, who had retired as Deputy Superintendents of Police, guilty of illegally detaining Gopi and sentenced them to one year rigorous imprisonment.

Gopi, a mosaic worker and captain of the village Kabaddi team, was charged by the duo with theft and was taken to the police station on October 17. When Thankappan went to meet his son he was not allowed inside. The following day, the policemen informed him that Gopi had committed suicide and he could collect the body from the local hospital.

After preserving his son's body in the concrete tank, Thankappan petitioned for a probe alleging that Gopi's death under mysterious circumstances at the police station was the fallout of a spat with a police constable during a Kabaddi match and the theft charge was fabricated.

Gopi's death was probed by both the Crime Branch and the CBI and was reported as suicide. While Gopi's body lay in the tank, his father ran from door to door for justice. It was only the High Court order to probe all aspects of Gopi's illegal detention that made the old man finally cremate his son.

While the legal battle was on Thankappan died in 2005. "Gopi was killed by the policemen no matter what the inquiry reports revealed. It was common knowledge. It did not help our cause that many witnesses in the case turned hostile. His father was heartbroken after fighting so long for justice," said Gopi's mother Janaki.

Heading: Bhopal seeks more aid, memorial for gas victims - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP Government on Thursday decided to withdraw its two-day-old order directing all temples under the purview of the Muzrai Department to perform pujas in the name of Karnataka's new Chief Minister.

Following a Cabinet meeting on Thursday, Home Minister V S Acharya announced that a decision had been taken to withdraw the June 9 circular of the Religious and Charitable Endowments Department asking for prayers in the name of Chief Minister B S Yeddyurappa. "Since the CM already has the blessing of the five crore people of Karnataka, a decision has been taken to withdraw the circular," Acharya said.

The June 9 circular, made public by Muzrai Department Minister Krishnaiah Setty on June 11, without naming Yeddyurappa, stated pujas must be performed in the names of the CM and his Government everyday. The circular, issued by the Muzrai Commissioner, said: "It is directed by the Muzrai Minister that for overall development of the state and for welfare of the people, to maintain peace and tranquillity, all the Muzrai temples in the state should perform 'archana' in the name of the Chief Minister and Government." Nearly 30,000 temples come under the purview of the department.

BJP leaders said the circular was not being withdrawn because it had embarrassed the new Government. Similar circulars had been issued during the tenure of the Congress and JD(S) governments specifically mentioning the names of the CMs, BJP leaders said.

Heading: The third angle - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 25 years after the Bhopal Gas tragedy, Madhya Pradesh is asking the Centre to declare 20 wards as "gas affected" and hence liable for compensation. The last compensation was paid in 1999 from the 470 million dollars that Union Carbide paid.

In addition to this, at the Group of Ministers meeting on Wednesday, the state asked the Centre for Rs 982 crore to rehabilitate gas victims. They have also asked for Rs 40 crore to convert the 67 square-acre factory site into a memorial park with a 'Ground Zero' that would have a statue of a "wailing lady".

"The Centre passed the National Disaster Act in 1984 and took up the guardianship of the Bhopal gas victims. Since 1999, they have not paid a penny to the state," Babu Lal Gaur, minister in-charge of the Bhopal Gas Relief Department told The Indian Express.

Of the total 56 wards in the city, 36 were considered to be gas affected. People from the remaining 20 had to prove that they suffered due to the gas leak to be eligible for relief. Only 15,000 people in these 20 wards got compensation. "Just because people stay on the other side of the road does not mean that they do not qualify for compensation," said Gaur.

Union Carbide had paid 470 million dollars to the Indian government in 1989 in a settlement reached after a protracted legal battle. On an average, the victims got Rs 25,000 in case of illness and the relatives of those who died got Rs 100,000.

The state government has passed a resolution in the assembly declaring the 20 wards to be gas affected. They now want the Centre to pay for their compensation.

While the state pleaded for additional funds, they strongly opposed the idea of the Commission that the Prime Minister recently announced. The state government has opposed it on the grounds that there are two monitoring committees appointed by the Supreme Court and there can be no other body larger than this. They stressed that assistance in the form of money was all that they required and not another commission.

Arjun Singh, the chairman of the Group of Ministers, is likely to take a decision on the state's request. The other members of the GOM are Ram Vilas Paswan, Prithviraj Chauhan, Sis Ram Ola and Oscar Fernandes.

Gaur, representing his state, presented a detailed plan of what the memorial will look like. The attempt is to connect the locked-and-barred site with the rest of the city. Its 'ground zero' will be preserved for posterity. There will be a glass-encased exhibition site, labs, a school, hostel, conference hall and an auditorium. The total estimate given by a Delhi-based architect for the plan is Rs 90 crore. The state has already sanctioned Rs 10 crore towards it and is asking the Centre for the remainder. Meanwhile, a group of activists have been camping in Delhi for the last two months demanding a Commission and legal action against Dow. In a bid to placate the protesters, the PMO had last month sent an emissary to the victims with an assurance that the Centre would comply with their demand and set up the commission.

Since it did not mention powers, funds and the term of the Commission, the activists have rejected the demand and are now on a hunger strike. Twenty-three of them are in jail for protesting outside the PMO.

The state government dismissed this group, saying they did not represent the victims and were only trying to "put the government in the dock".

Heading: Lavish in protest - Indian Express
Content:
Aditi Sharma and Udit Bharati were in their teens when they met and fell in love. Their courtship continued through their student years in Mahantsingh Engineering College and when their parents learnt about the relationship they readily agreed to the marriage.

Life couldn't have got any better. They postponed their plans for marriage as both wanted to acquire an MBA degree and secured admission at the Indian Institute of Modern Management at Wakad in Pune, unaware that their lives were about to change drastically.

The couple, both 25, arrived in Pune in 2006 and while Aditi began staying at the ladies hostel of the institute, Udit and a few friends moved into an apartment. Soon, Aditi met Pravin Khandelwal, a 25 year-old youth from Jaipur and fell for him, heedless of her six-year old relationship with Udit. Madly in love with Pravin, she reportedly told Udit that she was no longer interested in pursuing a relationship with him.

According to A.K. Bharati, Udit's father, encouraged by Aditi, Pravin confronted Udit warning him to not interfere in his (Pravin's) and Aditi's relationship. "In a call that he made to his mother in the October of 2006, Udit told his mother that the relationship between him and Aditi no longer existed. He also told her that Pravin had confronted him, asking him to stay away from them," said Bharati.

While Udit, a top ranker in his class continued with his management studies, Aditi and Pravin moved to Gurgaon in search of work. Six months passed and Aditi came back into Udit's life again. She made a call to his cell phone, asking him to meet her at a restaurant in Chinchwad. When the estranged couple met on the evening of April 22, allegedly in the presence of Pravin, Aditi is said to have offered her former lover prasad from the Shirdi Sai Baba shrine.

After the meeting, Udit returned to his flat where he began vomiting. His friends rushed him to hospital, where he died a couple of days later. The post mortem revealed traces of arsenic in Udit's body, which was attributed to the prasad. Udit's parents began to see links between the break-up with Aditi and his death. Suspecting that Aditi and Pravin had planned his son's murder, Bharati filed a case of murder against the two. Udit's friends provided an important clue in the case when they informed the police that a day after Udit was hospitalised, a girl had called on his cell phone. His friend who had received the call suspected that the girl was Aditi.

While a strong motive for the murder still seems hazy with the couple refusing to divulge or confess anything, police inspector Bajirao Mohite of the Hinjewadi police station said the basic motive was the girl's desire to not let anything mar her newfound relationship. "We suspect Aditi did not want her past to haunt her and hence wanted to get Udit out of the way, lest he interferes in her life with Pravin. While its possible that after the break-up Udit may have made attempts to speak to her, it's also a fact that he changed his cell phone number, probably in an attempt to forget her," said Mohite.

The police arrested Aditi and Pravin on May 16, 2007. While they confirmed that Aditi had broken off with Udit after she met Pravin, they denied murdering him. While Pravin was let off on bail after a month, Aditi was refused bail being the prime accused in the case as she had allegedly killed Udit by giving him the prasad. The case came up for hearing at the district sessions court, Pune, roughly a year after the murder.

On June 11, Additional Sessions Judge S S Phansalkar-Joshi held Aditi and Pravin guilty of Udit's murder. On June 12, the judge sentenced them to undergo rigorous life imprisonment and pay a fine of Rs 10,000 each.

"It was Pravin who must have devised the murder plot with Aditi merely executing it. Pravin had even issued threats to Udit when he began seeing Aditi. Aditi's family and ours have known each other for six years and we had already accepted her as our daughter-in-law. In fact if she would have even told us about Udit after he was dead and expressed her apology, the case would probably not have come even this far, " said Udit's father A.K. Bharati, who works for Canara Bank in Jammu. He and his wife live in the posh Trikuta Nagar locality of Jammu.

Aditi's parents are both doctors who live in Sainik Colony area of Jammu.

While the Bharatis were not at home, Udit's aunt, Dr Rajni Bharati, a doctor at the Government Medical College Hospital, said, "It was a very tragic end for my brother's son. But we are happy with the verdict."

With inputs from Jammu

Heading: Who are the Amra Bangalis? - Indian Express
Content:
There's something about the Gurjjar protest at Pilupura that jars—here, among the protestors is a group of people agitating for a cause they hope will bring the community more jobs and get them out of poverty but nothing about their lifestyle points to their modest cause.

A little distance from where Gurjjar leader Kirori Singh Bainsala sits, is a grey jeep and a few meters further away is a black Pajero and a red Tavera. Inside another SUV, sits Bainsala's advocate, busy with his laptop as he punches in a demand letter that the Gurjjars would present to the government. One of the Gurjjar leaders is heard talking on the phone: "Aam aa gaya market main? Dus ek kilo top class aam mangvaiye. Ab apko batane ki zaroort to nahi ki kis ke liye mangwa rahe hai (Bring in at least 10 kg of high-quality mangoes. I am sure you know who to send it to)."

The makeshift clinic at the site is well stocked. All the Gurjjars who make decisions are the ones who zip around in SUVs, not the ones baking in the sun.

The only woman Gurjjar leader among the protestors is Manju Singh, who doesn't follow the local Gurjjar dialect. She speaks in Hindi.

And then, there are people like Ram Bir Singh Bhiduri, the Delhi Congress MLA from Badarpur who goes around in his SUV, giving media persons sound bytes by generously rolling down the windows of his air-conditioned car.

But there are other Gurjjars leaders who are not from such elitist backgrounds. Captain Harprasad Tanwar, who is second in command to Bainsala, retired from the Rajput regiment as a captain. One of his two sons is a nursing assistant and the other is a peon in the army canteen. In the crowd there are women for whom the only sign of prosperity is the three gold dots on their teeth which they proudly show off. One group of Gurjjar agitators crowds food trolleys for their share of rabri—a dessert—while the other passes expensive packs of cigarettes around.

But Bainsala represents the other class—the English-speaking, affluent section of Gurjjars (his granddaughter studies in Mayo College). "I will open my Chivas Regal the day we get the recommendation letter. I have not touched that bottle in 22 years," he says, bristling with pride.

Heading: New combination pill for groups prone to malaria - Indian Express
Content:
As trains pull into West Bengal, passengers find the station names in Hindi and English smeared with black tar, leaving only the Bengali version visible. That's about the highest visibility secured so far by Amra Bangali, a radical pro-Bengali group that has now imposed a bandh in Siliguri and Dooars in protest against the demand for Gorkhaland.

On Thursday, the Amra Bangali, together with the Banglabhasha Bachao Samiti and Jana Jagaran Morcha, managed to bring Siliguri to a halt with its bandh call.

The group—that says it's important to speak Bengali and adapt to Bengali ways to live in what it calls "Bangali-stan"—is not restricted to West Bengal but to some parts of neighbouring states and even countries where Bengalis have immigrated to.

Sparked off by the 1983 Assam movement better known to Bengalis as the "Bongali Kheda" or "Drive away Bengalis" movement, Amra Bangali enjoyed a short stint in the spotlight in the mid-eighties when it even won some gram panchayat seats in border districts.

It is a frontal organisation of the Ananda Marg, the sworn enemies of the CPI(M). Amra Bangali was set up by Prabhat Ranjan Sarkar, who set up the Ananda Marg. Over the years, its physical presence has all but disappeared as mainstream Leftists promoted some other outfits that made strident calls to promote the use of Bengali and the cause of the Bengalis.

Amra Bangali never became violent or "exclusive", but its demands are radical. It wants a Bengal that is a self-contained socio-economic zone with people speaking the same language and wearing the same attire. There should be no imports into the region—and no export of raw materials either.

The Bangalistan envisioned by the group would include parts of Assam, plains of Meghalaya, West Bengal, Tripura, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Bihar and Jharkhand. In fact, its territorial ambitions are international—it wants Nepal's Jhapa district, Myanmar's Arakan area, and the whole of Bangladesh.

Heading: Two RTI courses in Mumbai law college from this session - Indian Express
Content:
In what could prove to be a huge relief for the troops posted in the border areas, Northeast and millions of people vulnerable to the malaria threat, the National Institute of Malaria Research (NIMR) has successfully completed clinical trials of a combination of drugs that could be taken in just one capsule.

The malaria parasite has become so resistant to chloroquine, the standard drug for preventing the disease, that high-risk areas like the Northeast, Jharkhand, Orissa and West Bengal have stopped prescribing the medicine.

Instead, these states are now relying on Artemisinin derivative-based Combination Therapy (ACT), which is believed to be effective in case of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum (PF) malaria, which contributes to 50 per cent of the total cases in the country.

The NIMR, after the trials, have also recommended the use of other combination drugs like artesunate and amodiaquine, artesunate and methoquine, artesunate and pyronaridine, dih droartemisinin and piperaquine.

Dr A P Dash, director, NIMR told The Indian Express that the researchers at the institute have successfully tested these new combination drugs.

Dr Neena Valecha, senior deputy director, NIMR, said that the institute will submit its recommendations to the Drugs Controller General of India (DGCI) for approval. The new combination drugs can be taken in fixed doses in just one tablet, said Valecha. She, however, pointed out that the patient must be diagnosed with PF malaria to be administered the drugs.

Heading: Rs 58-cr joint rural health programme with US launched - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai's K C Law College, recognised by the Bar Council of India, will be the first law institute in India to introduce two courses on Right to Information.

The courses, which will begin this academic session beginning July, are being offered at two levels — foundation and advanced.

College principal Neelima Chandiramani, who is the brainchild behind these certificate courses says, the common man should be able to make good use of RTI and sloppily drafted applications will never yield information.

While the syllabus of the foundation course will comprise history of the Act, its provisions and case studies, the advanced-level is designed for citizens who know the basics but need to learn certain 'tricks' such as ways to ask for information when the government or a department tries to hoodwink a person by giving excuses.

We want to train candidates in such a way that if they become information commissioners, they understand the problem," said Chandiramani, who took up this project together with RTI activist Shailesh Gandhi. Gandhi and information commissioner V V Kovlikar will be taking sessions during the weekend. The classes will run into five sessions, each three hours long and priced at Rs 2,000 for basic and advanced levels.

Heading: Centre hikes paddy MSP to Rs 850 - Indian Express
Content:
Aiming to improve maternal and child mortality rate in the country, the Health and Family Welfare Ministry along with the US Government on Thursday launched a Rs 58 crore programme for rural India.

The initiative is a US-India partnership comprising India Clinical Epidemiology Network, Population Foundation of India, Public Health Foundation of India, Emerging Market Group and Boston University. "We need an expanding reservoir of professional research, public health and technical assistance institutions working at global standards that can support government programmes," the USAID release said.

The programme will specifically focus on the states of Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand and other economically backward states in North India.The Maternal and Child Health Sustainable Technical Assistance and Research Initiative (MCH-Star) will work to improve maternal and child health care in India over the next five years through applied research, policy analysis, advocacy and technical assistance.

Singling out lack of trained manpower and other institutional mechanisms as key reasons behind the depressing health statistics in these states, USAID Mission Director George Deikun said the programme would both supplement and complement the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM).

Initially, USAID will fund the entire project. However, its contribution will come down to 10 per cent of the total cost by the end of five years as the partnering agencies will take over the cost.

Heading: Chhattisgarh BJP faces heat over partyman’s graft charge - Indian Express
Content:
In the face of rising prices of consumer goods and a mounting subsidy bill, the Government on Thursday failed short of living up to its self-proclaimed 'pro-farmer' credential and resorted to an "ad hoc" arrangement in fixing the minimum support price (MSP) for paddy for the ensuing kharif season. It deferred a decision on the MSP for other crops.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), which met on Thursday, raised the MSP for normal grade paddy by Rs 105 to Rs 850 per quintal for this year as an ad hoc measure before leaving the matter to the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council (EAC) for final decision on increasing it to Rs 1,000 as recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP). The CACP had recommended a Rs 255 hike in the MSP from Rs 745 a quintal for common variety paddy.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Finance Minister P Chidambaram said the EAC had not been given any time-frame to suggest its recommendations and added that they would come up "as soon as possible". "Some states like Gujarat, MP and Orissa wanted less than Rs 1,000 a quintal as MSP, while others wanted more. In view of the divergent views, the matter was referred to the Prime Minister's EAC."

"Certainly, the fact that prices are high in the retail market has gone into consideration in announcing the MSP," replied Chidambaram in response to a question whether rising consumer prices factored into not accepting the CACP recommendations.

Sources, in fact, said the argument of "divergent views" among states over this issue was an alibi being used by the Government to control the prices from crashing through the roof when the country is heading towards general elections. While the rising prices forced the Government to balk at raising paddy MSP, rising fertiliser subsidy bill forced the CCEA to accept shifting from existing product-based subsidy regime to nutrient-based subsidy regime.

Unlike the existing regime where only selected fertilisers are eligible for concessions, under the new regime all fertiliser products will be eligible for subsidy based on their nutrient value. The new regime will bring the prices of complex fertilisers down by an average of Rs 70 per bag.

Heading: Bhattal cites attack on Hindu families, wants BJP to dump SAD - Indian Express
Content:
As the ruling BJP in Chhattisgarh gears up for the Assembly polls in November this year, veteran tribal leader Baliram Kashyap has put the party in a tight spot by alleging that a few BJP legislators and even office-bearers were indulging in fund-raising through unfair means, even by misusing the Right to Information Act.

"These MLAs and office-bearers are tarnishing the image of the party. I have prepared a list of such party functionaries which I would submit to the party high command," Kashyap, a senior-most tribal BJP leader and Member of Parliament, told mediapersons in Bastar on Wednesday evening.

"It's just a loot. Their modus operandi is simple: file applications under RTI, and later collect money from government officers and employees," he said, adding if the situation continued, it would be difficult for the party to win elections in the Bastar region.

The statement of Kashyap, whose son Kedar is the Minister of State for Public Health Engineering in the Raman Singh Government, has ruffled many feathers. A group of tribal legislators, comprising Women and Child Welfare Minister Lata Usendi, legislators Subhau Kashyap and Lachuram Kashyap and a few party office-bearers from Bastar, called on state organising secretary Ram Pratap Singh and urged him to restrain the senior tribal leader from making such statements.

These leaders have also brought the matter to the notice of Dharmendra Pradhan, who is in charge of party affairs in the state, and Chief Minister Raman Singh.

State BJP president Vishnu Deo Sai refused to comment on Kashyap's statement, saying the party would take note of it after talking to the tribal leader. "Kashyap is one of our senior-most leaders. If he says something, others should take it in the right spirit", he added.

The Congress was quick to react, saying the tribal leader's remarks had exposed the BJP Government. "Kashyap's statement also indicates that BJP legislators are on a weak wicket, and they are not in a position to win the elections," said state Congress president Dhanendra Sahu, adding they would make corruption a major issue in the elections.

However, the CM dismissed the charges as baseless. "With Assembly polls just six months away, a demoralised and confused Opposition is just trying to find a suitable election plank," he added.

Heading: Rs 29-crore relief for Bhagalpur riots victims - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress on Thursday accused the BJP of playing votebank politics and being a silent spectator to the growing religious fundamentalism, especially incidence of violence against Hindus in Punjab. Comparing the present situation in the state to militancy days in the 1980s, Punjab Congress chief Rajinder Kaur Bhattal sought Central intervention.

According to Bhattal, 15 Hindu families from Magh village in Amritsar district, who were participating in "jagrata" (a nightlong religious ceremony) last Tuesday, were attacked by anti-social elements forcing the families to take shelter in Durgiana temple in Amritsar.

"The BJP and Lal Krishna Advaniji should explain why they continue to be a part of the government, which is doing nothing to protect the Hindus. If they (BJP) sympathise with the Hindus they should withdraw their support to the state government," Bhattal told reporters here.

She cited several incidents to substantiate her claim that the SAD-BJP regime was indifferent to growing religious fundamentalism in the state. For instance, she said, Jathedar Joginder Singh Vedanti had recently endorsed the idea of Khalistan in New York recently, but the Akali Government did not condemn it. Vedanti had later denied making any such statement, though. Earlier, there was an attempt to create religious polarization over the controversy surrounding Dera Sacha Sauda sect, said Bhattal.

Accusing the SAD-BJP Government of unleashing a reign of terror, she said, "There has been a series of violent incidents in Punjab, be it a result of political rivalry during elections or deteriorating law and order situation. There have been several incidents involving attack on religious minorities. There has always been a separatist tendency in the state. If you stoke it, it could spin out of control. This is a dangerous trend."

Bhattal had met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh early this week to apprise him of the situation and said. She reached New Delhi on Thursday seeking an appointment with Home Minister Shivraj Patil for the same.

The Congress has three suggestions for the Centre: seek a report about the present situation from the state; Union Home Minister should call the Chief Minister and talk to him; or the Centre should send a team to Punjab to study the situation.

Bhattal sought to play down her differences with former CM Capt Amarinder Singh. "He says he is not well. There could be some personal reason. I have no differences with him. I want that he should also come together with us. Our Party is one. Our Leader is one. We have the same outlook. I don't think he is not coming to us deliberately. He may have some compulsions," said the PCC chief.

Heading: Congress panel split over projecting CM nominees - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre on Thursday announced a Rs 29.81-crore relief and rehabilitation package for the next of kin of those killed and injured in the Bhagalpur riots of 1989 in Bihar. The package was approved by the Union Cabinet at its meeting chaired by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. The announcement came in less than a month after the Centre came out with a similar package for the 2002 Gujarat riots victims.

Under the relief package for Bhagalpur riot victims, an ex gratia of Rs 3.5 lakh will be paid to the next of kin of each of the 844 persons killed, an official spokesman told reporters after the meeting.

He said the relief amount would be in addition to what has been paid by the state Government and added that this would entail an expenditure of Rs 29.54 crore to the exchequer.

A sum of up to Rs 1.25 lakh would be given to 22 injured persons, but the amount would be adjusted against what has been paid by the state Government. This would entail an expenditure of Rs 26.99 lakh.

However, the compensation announced for the Bhagalpur riots victims fell short of being at par with that paid to victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots as the Government did not announce any compensation for residential properties damaged during the riots.

Government sources said lack of data regarding the damaged residential properties was the main reason for not announcing the compensation for the same. They said the state Government was yet to provide the relevant data to the Centre.

Heading: Buta: UP has worst record of atrocities on Dalits - Indian Express
Content:
With a section of the Congress pinning the blame for the party's successive electoral reverses on a "faceless" campaign, a high-level committee, set up to plan a roadmap for the party for the forthcoming Assembly and parliamentary elections, on Thursday discussed the pros and cons of projecting a chief ministerial candidate before the elections.

The A K Antony-led committee, which met here, could not reach a conclusion though, said party sources. Party leaders were of the view that projecting a CM candidate, especially when he or she lacks mass appeal, could result in the common man identifying the party with a particular caste or community. This could be counter-productive. Besides, the Congress did not have the tradition of projecting a CM candidate in elections. The counter view that has gained currency following the party's reverses in Gujarat and Karnataka is that the voters are reluctant to cast their vote for a 'faceless' party.

Members were also of the view that the party should announce its candidates for elections much in advance. AICC general secretaries Digvijay Singh and Mukul Wasnik would prepare a draft report, which would be approved by the committee at its final meeting on June 21.

Heading: BJP’s UP strategy draws on heavyweights, ties with RLD - Indian Express
Content:
National Commission for Scheduled Castes chairman Buta Singh on Thursday said Uttar Pradesh had the worst track record when it comes to atrocities on Dalits. Singh was heading a three-member fact-finding team of the commission to Kanti village, where the police allegedly used force on June 7 to evict Dalits from a plot which had been recently sold.

"Uttar Pradesh continues to be at the top in terms of the number of cases of atrocities against Dalits reported in states across the country. The latest data available with us is for 2006 when the state recorded a whopping 52,827 such cases," Singh said.

He said the backward classes were being driven to the wall in the state "due to an unsympathetic administration which has scant respect for the constitutional provisions made for the weaker sections".

"Mayawati has apparently has no control over the administration and the police as a result of which her proclaimed commitment to the cause of the Dalits was now under scanner," the former Union minister said.

After recording the statements of the villagers in Kanti, the commission termed the incident barbaric and ghastly. Singh said the role played by the district administration and the police was dubious, adding that the police did not even spare pregnant women and children. "The commission has taken the matter very seriously," he said, adding that he would recommend action against 40 police personnel including some officers.

Heading: 25 women get bail, Gurjjar team heads for Jaipur talks - Indian Express
Content:
After setting into motion the exercise to identify candidates for the forthcoming general elections, the Bharatiya Janata Party is exploring options to maximise its gains in Uttar Pradesh. As of now, the party is in the dumps in the state which sends as many as 80 members to the Lok Sabha.

One proposal said to have been discussed with party's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani entails dividing the state into six "clusters" and putting political heavyweights like Murli Manohar Joshi, Kalyan Singh, Kalraj Mishra, Maneka Gandhi and Yogi Adityanath in charge of each. Party general secretary Arun Jaitley, who played a key role in crafting the Karnataka win, may be asked to coordinate.

"When general elections are increasingly becoming an aggregate of local elections, it's important to have a national perspective. This arrangement will also ensure micromanagment of the elections besides imparting a national perspective to the campaign," said a source. State BJP organising secretary Nagendra met Advani recently to discuss the proposal.

The proposal defines a cluster (comprising 10 to 14 Lok Sabha seats) as having "common caste groups or communities". This will help in combining the Lok Sabha campaign with local and primordial concerns. Leaders identified with caste groups may be asked to focus on clusters where they wield considerable influence or where their caste constitute a majority.

The western UP cluster, with 15 seats, is dominated by the Jats. The two clusters in the east with 26 seats have Thakurs, Bhumihars and Muslims as dominant groups. The Bundelkhand cluster has Lodhis, Dalits and Kurmis, while the one around Farukahabad has Yadavs and Lodhis as dominant communities.

The RSS has divided the state into six zones — Gorakhpur, Kashi (eastern UP), Avadh, Kanpur, Braj and Pashcim (western UP), a classification that has been used by the BJP in the past as well. The party had deputed heavyweights from outside in all six zones in the last Assembly elections, but results showed that the arrangement didn't help. "We must have heavyweights identified with the local milieu. They should be able to match caste / regional aspirations with a national perspective," said a leader.

Another proposal is a tie-up with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal which wields considerable influence in western UP. While Ajit Singh, talking to The Indian Express on Thursday, denied the possibility of any such deal, one of his deputies confirmed that talks were on and the party had identified a "list of seats".

The BJP's Mission Delhi would come a cropper if it fails to improve its tally in UP. Party leader Kalyan Singh had recently said unless the party wins "25-30 states" in the state, "it can forget about its onward march to Delhi".

Heading: Chouhan cycle ride now more than a protest - Indian Express
Content:
The deadlock over second round of negotiations between agitating Gurjjars and the Rajasthan Government was broken on Thursday following the release of 25 arrested Gurjjar women on bail by the Dausa Sessions court. A delegation of Gurjjar leaders has already left for Jaipur by road to hold the talks.

At 12.30 pm, as the news poured in at Pilupura camp that the 25 women were granted bail, a crowd of Gurjjars present there broke into a cheerful mood. And after a brainstorming session, it was decided that a team of 27 members would hold talks with the Rajasthan Government in Jaipur.

At 5 pm, Superintendent of Police C P Sharma, who has been a key mediator during the agitation, and Deputy SP Rameshwar Gujjar arrived with a bus at the Pilupura camp. Four key leaders from Pilupura — Bhim Singh Bhadana, Captain Sir Mortar Singh, Droop Singh and Bhura Bhagat — were taken in the bus. They were later put in a Marshal jeep at Bayana and were sent to Jaipur with a team of Rajasthan Police officers escorting them. The rest of the members of the team would join at Jaipur.

Gurjjar leader Kirori Singh Bainsla thanked the Government for releasing the women. "Right now, I am not going to Jaipur, but if these talks go well I would do so soon," Bainsla told reporters at Pilupura.

Other than the recommendation letter for the ST status, the Gurjjars will also be discussing the release of 15 Gurjjar protestors who were arrested on charges of murder from SMS Hospital in Jaipur while they were undergoing treatment. "The Government has assured us that they would be sent back to hospital. We want that all charges against every protestor be quashed," said Attar Singh, a Gurjjar leader.

There is, however, no let-up in the agitation. At Pilupura, the Gurjjars continued to block the railway tracks. The situation is same in Sikandara where the Gurjjars are holding up the Agra-Jaipur highway.

Heading: Left unmoved by PM’s pitch on n-deal - Indian Express
Content:
It's unclear how Congress chief ministers have responded to the Prime Minister's appeal for austerity measures, but Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan seems to have taken it rather seriously. He has been cycling to office since the beginning of this week.

So, while the Finance Department is busy finding out how the petroleum hike will impact the state's economy, Chouhan, lean and much fitter than most of his younger colleagues, is doing his bit by cutting down on expenditure. Chouhan's official residence is on Shyamla Hills and the Secretariat is located at Arera Hills three km away, which means he must negotiate steep slopes either way.

Unlike his ministerial colleagues, the 47-year-old CM has carried on after the inaugural, well-publicised protest undertaken immediately after the petroleum products became dearer.

But barring two ministers, the rest have showed no desire to follow their leader. Senior minister Kailash Vijayvargiya went on a ride in Indore on Wednesday, but with his entire cavalcade following him the purpose of the effort was defeated. Ramdayal Ahirwar, a new minister, also cycled his way to office a couple of days ago, but he was making a virtue out of necessity. His official vehicle broke down at the last moment and it would have been difficult to arrange a new vehicle with a red beckon.

Chouhan, however, has bought a new cycle for Rs 2,500. Unlike Vijayvargiya, he will use the same mode on the way back, keeping all cars parked at his residence. The CM is known to walk long distances during poll campaigns, earning for himself the sobriquet of "Paon Paon Vale Bhaiyya".

The security personnel, who flank him during the ride, are getting new cycles as the CM insists the weekly rides will continue till he is in office. In fact, the CM, who anyway has minimal security, has asked the Intelligence Department to suggest ways to cut down on vehicles in his official cavalcade. He has also suggested that barring the collector and the SP other officials in districts explore new ways to reach official venues, preferably in a bus.

The Congress, meanwhile, has dismissed it as a drama.

Heading: Renuka wants tighter guidelines for children working in showbiz - Indian Express
Content:
Despite Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's statement on Wednesday that the nuclear deal is in India's strategic interest, the CPI(M) on Thursday said it would give its nod only when its apprehensions regarding the deal were cleared.

Talking to mediapersons, CPI(M) Politburo member Sitaram Yechury said the Left continues to have "apprehensions and objections" with regard to the deal. However, he maintained that it's opposition was mainly against the 123 Agreement and against safeguards agreement with the IAEA. "Our objection is not with IAEA. Our objection is with the 123 Agreement, which according to us is very deeply anchored in the Hyde Act (of the US)," Yechury said.

Asked whether the Left would allow signing of the safeguards agreement if the Government delinks it from the 123 pact, Yechury said the party's response would depend on the Government's explanation. "It all depends on what the Government says in the next meeting. Let the Government say that," he said. The UPA-Left coordination committee will meet on June 18 to discuss whether the Government should go ahead with signing the safeguards agreement with the IAEA. Repeating his party's known position, Yechury said the Hyde Act, under which the US can have civil nuclear cooperation with India, has "many features which are objectionable and not acceptable, with regard to India's sovereignty".

On the Prime Minister's comments on Wednesday, Yechury said Singh had only reiterated his known position on the deal. Pitching for the deal, Singh said it was crucial for India's strategic interests and an end to the "nuclear apartheid" against the country. Singh allayed apprehensions that it would compromise the country's interests.

Heading: Maoists, Muslim fundamentalists to fight ‘state terror’ together - Indian Express
Content:
From now on, it will not be easy for film and TV serial producers to recruit children in the showbiz. "They will have to adhere to certain guidelines and make sure that children are working under proper conditions," said Minister for Women and Child Development (WCD) Renuka Chowdhury on the occasion of the World Day Against Child Labour on Thursday.

The Minister has directed the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) to frame guidelines in this regard. The NCPCR will soon form a committee comprising representatives from the Women and Child Development Ministry, NCPCR, Labour Ministry, Health Ministry and psychologists who will work on the guidelines. "Parents think if their children are working, it adds to their profile. What's important here is to see under which conditions their children are working. Kids perform like animals. This will not be tolerated," said Chowdhury. "There should be a law to check this."

According to the UN convention, children should work only four hours a day. However, the NCPCR has got to know the children are made to work during night hours. "Once the guidelines are framed, surprise checks will be conducted in the states where the programmes are shot at. The main aim is to ensure that children should not be made to overwork," said Sandhya Bajaj, member, NCPCR. The members will check if the children are getting proper food while they work, whether the food is nutritious and whether working timings are fine.

Chowdhury said she would also soon talk to the I and B Minister about the kind of advertisements shown during the programmes meant for children. "We have seen that ads which are telecast during the children's programmes at times do not match kids' frame of mind. It should be taken care of," she added.

The Minister said if she had her way, she would have announced capital punishment for those employing child labour. "It's shameful on our part to recruit children as domestic help. Police verification should not be confined to checking their criminal record but it should also check their age," she added.

Chowdhury, in fact, came up with a slew of measures to curb child labour — there are 12.5 million children employed as labour, according to her Ministry. "I'll talk to the HRD minister and make sure that flexibility is shown to the children who want to study, irrespective of their age," she said.

She will also speak to Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia and request him to allocate money to states after checking their women and child fund allocation. "This will ensure that states are doing enough for them," she added.

Heading: Clinton Climate Initiative joins hands with Indian group to retrofit buildings - Indian Express
Content:
Maoists and Muslim fundamentalists — they may seem to be the most unlikely partners. But in a move which is rife with much internal contradictions and political ramifications, the two are coming together to forge a national platform to combat "state terror".

Calling themselves "the victims of state terror", the two improbable partners had sat together for the first time and called for resistance against all kinds of terror unleashed by the State and Central governments against Maoists and Muslims. The meeting was held in Kerala last month.

The main forces behind the move are — 'Porattom', a Maoist group having base in South India, Minority Watch, a human rights organisation suspected of having close links with the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) and National Democratic Front (NDF), a radical Muslim group accused of having similar links with the banned Islamic Sevak Sangh (ISS).

"Maoists and Muslims share the similar plight of being the victims of the state terror. The best way to eliminate anyone who raises his voice against the wrong doings of the State is to brand him as a Naxalite. Similar is the plight of Muslim brethren. Whenever and wherever there is a terrorist attack, the community as a whole is brought under the eye of suspicion. Every Muslim is being treated as a potential terrorist. It is in this background that we have decided to join hands to combat this state sponsored terrorism," said Ravunni, general convener of Porattom.

Nazaruddeen Elamarom of the NDF also echoed similar views. "The Maoists and the Muslims are the worst affected victims of state terror. We are the favourite whipping boys of the Government as we are clubbed together as anti-nationals. And this is the common thread that connects the two," he said. According to him, it is for the first time that the Naxalites and Muslim groups are coming together for espousing a similar cause.

Nazarudden maintained that the fight would be against the upper caste ruling elite forces of Hindutva and imperialism who have the agenda of hunting down Maoists and Muslims. "This is for upholding human rights and to stop the fascists," he added.

The agenda of the Maoist-Muslim joint platform group includes withdrawal of ban on SIMI and a total full stop to encounter killings. They also want the Naxalites to be given the treatment of war prisoners.

According to Ravunni, they are in touch with many other Maoist and Muslim groups across the country. "We are planning to hold our next meetings in Bangalore and Calcutta. We would be deciding upon the nature and structure of the joint platform in those meetings and it would have a pan Indian nature," he said. Ravunni said that the meeting has brought together two victim groups together and the rest of the fight would be fought together.

Acknowledging that it was an unlikely alliance, Ravunni said: "A lot of complexities are involved in this coming together." "But we would unite to fight against the common enemy putting aside differences in their ideologies," he added.

The meeting was also attended by some civil society movements including Confederation of Human Rights Organisation (CHRO) and People's Union Civil Liberty (PUCL) working against encounter killings and anti-terror laws.

Heading: Sriperambudur airport set for early take-off - Indian Express
Content:
Marking the biggest and first of its kind tie-up in the private sector, Real Estate major K Raheja Corp is working with former US president Bill Clinton-led Clinton Climate Initiative (CCI) to retrofit their buildings across the country to cut Green House Gases. "Climate change is a global problem that requires local action," Bill Clinton had said on May 17 last year, while announcing the Energy Efficiency Building Retrofit Program which looks at retrofitting the larger buildings in sixteen of the world's largest cities.

Mumbai is one of the cities listed from India, where K Raheja Corp has started work on Inorbit Mall in Malad and a hotel in Powai, first in their list of 20 odd buildings to be retrofitted.

While the concept of constructing green buildings is fairly established, retrofitting existing new buildings is comparatively a new concept. And the real estate group, which plans to retrofit all its properties, is not only looking at cuts in energy bills but also at a savvy international image.

"We have signed a first-ever project development under the Clinton Climate Initiative and are working on the energy audit with Johnsons Control, one of the companies introduced as the leading energy efficiency provider by the CCI," says Shabbir Kanchwala, associate vice president, K Raheja Corp.

And it's not just about energy saving, he says. "Not only will we cut our energy expenditure by 20 to 25 per cent, but will also save up to 20 per cent water. Moreover, this is also building for the future as don't sell any of our properties. Instead, we lease them out to world renowned companies like Microsoft, which like to work in savvy, eco-friendly buildings. We are the first ones to retrofit our buildings, but we are also the first to gain this competitive edge," says Kanchwala.

Work has started in Mumbai and Hyderabad, and according to the company, 50 lakh square feet of built space (in over 20 odd buildings) will be retrofitted. For the process, smarter glass varieties (which let in light, not heat) and better suited air-conditioning systems are used. Sewage treatment is also done to conserve and recycle water.

While some government buildings have been retrofitted for cutting carbon emissions, the concept is still picking up in the private sector. "Many government buildings under the CPWD have been retrofitted, like the Rashtrapati Bhawan and the Prime Minister's Office (PMO). The concept is catching up now in the private sector as retrofitting to cut emissions is a win-win situation," says Sanjay Seth, Energy Economist, Bureau of Energy Efficiency.

Heading: Nine more entries in hazardous list under Child Labour Act - Indian Express
Content:
Chennai's proposed greenfield airport is set for an early start, with the Tamil Nadu Government on Thursday making it clear that it would not be able to assure the Centre on the availability of land for the Phase II expansion of the existing airport at Meenambakkam.

According to sources, the Chennai airport's capacity will be saturated by 2015-16 if the Phase II expansion for upgrading the existing infrastructure does not come through. The only option available to the Centre would be to expedite the process to build the greenfield airport at Sriperumbudur approximately 40 km from Chennai to meet passenger demand. The matter was brought up at a meeting between the Cabinet Secretary and the Ministry of Civil Aviation while reviewing the projects.

The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is already on the job with a techno-feasibility study done for the new airport and will soon get the reports of a study by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).

"Soon after the ICAO study is with AAI, a Detailed Project Report (DPR) will be prepared and with Government clearance land will be acquired for the greenfield airport. While a sort of go-ahead to expedite work on this project has come from the Cabinet Secretariat today, a formal clearance is also likely to follow soon", said a senior official from the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

The initial phase of the new airport will cost more than Rs 5,000 crore, say sources.

Heading: ‘My son being framed for marrying a Hindu girl’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a notification to amend the existing Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, the Union Ministry of Labour and Employment has added eight other hazardous processes and one occupation to the existing list of 72 processes and occupations which are prohibited under the Act.

The notification list includes processes involving exposure to free silica as in the case of slate and pencil industry, stone grinding, slate stone mining, agate industry and stone quarries. The occupation added to the list is diving.

The amended Act will also prohibit children below 14 years of age from working in mechanised fishing industries, timber handling and loading, food processing, beverage industry, mechanical lumbering and warehousing.

On Thursday, the ministry also issued a protocol laying down guidelines for rescue and rehabilitation of migrant child labourers.

The detailed protocol is based on a "multi-pronged approach" that includes government and community mobilisation and creation of suitable rehabilitation infrastructure.

According to government figures, about 1.2 million children between the age of five and 14 are employed as child labourers or marginal workers across all states in India. The protocol and the above amendments are expected to come into force by September this year.

Heading: Dasmunsi: cut-throat media competition is unhealthy - Indian Express
Content:
Even as 21-year-old Mudassar Irfan, a management trainee, was sent to 14 days of judicial custody for allegedly kidnapping Aditi Tyagi, his father said he was being framed for marrying a Hindu girl.

Aditi had gone missing on Monday evening, and her car was found drowned in Hindon River. Since the Ghaziabad Police could not find the girl's body, a missing report was converted into a case of suspected kidnapping. After tracing the girl's call details, the police arrested Mudassar who was returning from his office on Wednesday.

The police claimed the boy had been sent to judicial custody as the girl had told the court (in an in-camera statement) that she was drugged and kidnapped. "The girl told court that someone had drugged her and she became unconscious till the time police discovered her from Mudassar's room in Gurgaon," stated Ghaziabad SSP Deepak Ratan. This statement by the SSP is in contrast with his earlier statement given on Wednesday that both of them had married a year ago.

All attempts to contact Aditi failed.

However, Dr Irfan Ahmad, father of Mudassar who visited him in Dasna jail in Ghaziabad on Thursday, claimed his son was innocent. "We have not been given a chance to hire a lawyer," alleged Irfan. "Aditi and Mudassar are adults, so why was he sent to judicial custody on abduction charge when police on Wednesday had categorically told the media that, according to the girl, they had both got married a year ago?"

Dr Ahmad said, "Since it was impossible for them to get a place to live in after disclosing their real names, Mudassar had converted to Hinduism. Now, he is Manav," he added.

The father alleged the police had hidden a few details that could have proved Mudassar innocent. "My son told me the police had confiscated his mobile in which the proceedings of their registered marriage are recorded. They both got married on May 17, 2008, in Tees Hazari court," he added.

However, police sources said these details were not in the case diary.

After the medical check-up of the duo at MMG hospital, Ghaziabad, Mudassar's statement was recorded, and he was sent to judicial custody whereas Aditi's in-camera statements were recorded and she was handed over to the family.

Mudassar's bail application could not be forwarded to the court as the lawyers are on strike. "We are consulting our lawyer but have to wait till Monday, or till the strike is over," said the father.

Heading: US Consulate clarifies, says advisory for first-time visitors - Indian Express
Content:
Minister of Information and Broadcasting P R Dasmunsi on Thursday said the cut-throat competition amongst media groups was "unhealthy".

Speaking at the 41st convocation at the Indian Institute for Mass Communication (IIMC), the minister said while he was all for a free media, the current situation was a "matter of serious concern". "I strongly believe in free media but freedom demands responsibility. Overall, I appreciate the role of Indian media in nation-building and strengthening the roots of democracy. But unfortunately, the growing competition among media companies, if I may call it unhealthy competition, is threatening all journalistic norms and values," he said.

"My ministry is receiving many complaints from the public and concerned citizen groups. There are numerous instances of media excesses and media trials, fake sting operations, criminal trespassing of privacy, glamourisation of criminals and mafia dons, promotion of hatred among communities and inflaming of raw emotions. This is a dangerous trend not only for the media but also for democracy and all humanity," he added.

Asking the IIMC students to "have a constructive attitude and think in terms of solutions, not in terms of problems", the minister told them to remember that their job would entail "heavy responsibility in creating an informed and empowered citizenry". The minister noted that, according to recent industry reports, the Indian media and entertainment industry recorded a cumulative growth of 19 per cent in the last four years, and the sector will grow at a compound annual growth rate of 18 per cent in the next five years.

"This growth rate is almost unparalleled in the world. But to maintain and enhance this growth rate, the industry requires a large number of trained media professionals. I feel IIMC can play a greater role in providing good professionals. Therefore, IIMC needs to start new and specialised courses and training programmes geared to the needs of the industry," he said.

Heading: Cong bigwigs in Karnataka now eye RS seats - Indian Express
Content:
The US Consulate has written to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Council (BMC) chief stating that it has never prevented its citizens from coming to Mumbai.

On June 10, the US Consulate had put up an advisory on its website asking its citizens to be careful while navigating through the streets of Mumbai during the rains. The note, which talks about the BMC's inept handling of the waterlogging, had ruffled quite a few feathers in the civic corridors.

In his letter to Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak, US Consul General Michael Owen has clarified that the note was meant for those Americans coming to Mumbai for the first time and do not have any prior experience of the monsoon here. The letter in fact praises the BMC's "efficient" handling of the monsoon and floods every year. It also mentions that the consulate has in no way stopped anyone from coming here. In fact, it says, very soon, a group of US dignitaries will be on their way to Delhi and Mumbai.

Meanwhile, Mayor Shubha Raul has shot off a letter to the Consulate asking them to clarify the note on their website.

Heading: Air hostess suicide: pilot arrested, charged with abetment - Indian Express
Content:
Congress veterans from Karnataka may have failed to deliver the goods in the recent Assembly election, but they are lobbying hard to get party nominations for the biennial elections in the state for the four Rajya Sabha seats, scheduled on June 26.

Among the contenders are Veerappa Moily, Margaret Alva, Abdul Wahab, C K Jaffer Sharief, M V Rajashekaran (for renomination), S M Krishna, B K Chandrashekhar, and Anil Lad, among others, according to Congress sources.

Going by the parties' strength in the state Legislative assembly, the Congress could secure only one out of the four seats unless it ties up with the JD(S). The elections were necessitated following the retirement of Prema Cariappa, M V Rajashekaran, Vijay Mallya and Janardhana Poojary, whose terms had expired in April. However, election to fill the vacancies could not be held earlier in the absence of the electoral college.

The Congress and the JD(S) have 80 and 28 seats respectively in the state assembly. If the JD(S) were to support the Congress, the latter could get two seats. Congress sources said the JD(S) was "agreeable" to the idea of cooperation in Rajya Sabha election, but no formal talks have begun so far. The two sides are expected to start talks shortly, as the last date of making the nomination is June 16.

Congress sources said, former Karnataka Chief Minister Krishna stood a good chance to get the party nomination, as there were no Vokkaliga members from the Congress in the Rajya Sabha. But given Deve Gowda's apparent dislike for Krishna, the Congress would have to nominate the former Maharashtra Governor as its first choice so that he could romp home on the strength of Congress votes only. Krishna's failure to prove his political clout and mettle in the recent assembly election and his controversial utterances questioning the party strategy after the elections could, however, become a stumbling block in his nomination.

B K Chandrashekhar, Chairman of the Karnataka Legislative Council who retires on 30 June, is also said to be in the race. Congress MP Naveen Jindal's brother Sajjan Jindal's name was also doing the rounds in party circles as one of the prospective candidates for nomination.

Congress sources, however, said the Congress President Sonia Gandhi was yet to take a view on the issue. "She has been getting letters from various state Congress leaders to choose some fresh, 'faceless' candidates, instead of relying on old war horses. Don't be surprised if a new name is projected," said a senior Congress leader.

Heading: ‘Business as usual is no longer a viable option’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police on Thursday arrested a co-pilot with IndiGo and charged him with abetting the suicide of air hostess Sucheta Anand—who worked for the same airline—on Saturday night.

The Santacruz police booked Arjun Menon, a Powai resident, for abetment to suicide after recording the statements of 25-year-old Sucheta's parents.

Sucheta's body was found hanging from the ceiling fan of room no 311 in Hotel Palm Grove on June 7. According to the Santacruz police, Sucheta, a resident of the East of Kailash locality in New Delhi, arrived in Mumbai in the evening on Friday, June 6 and checked into the room booked by the airline after flight duty.

The police said Menon (30) was with her on the day — Saturday — she committed suicide. "In the evening, the attendant of the room knocked on the door for cleaning the room. When there was no response, the management opened the room with a duplicate key and found Sucheta hanging from the ceiling fan," said Senior Police Inspector Dilip Gaikwad of Santacruz police station.

Gaikwad added: "From what we have gathered so far, Sucheta and Menon, who is a divorcee, may have had a relationship. On the day she committed suicide, Menon was with her from morning till evening and two hours after he left, she committed suicide. This suggests that she was probably pushed to kill herself as a result of whatever transpired between them."

Heading: Judging the judges - Indian Express
Content:
The picture he paints is a frightening one but he also shows a way forward. Lester R. Brown, eco-environmentalist and author of 20 books on global environment issues, was in Delhi for the release of a Hindi translation of his book Plan B 3.0: Mobilizing to Save Civilization. It is a prescription on how to cut emissions by 80 per cent by 2020. The book talks about four overriding goals: to stabilise climate, stabilise population, eradicate poverty and restore the earth's damaged eco-systems. A failure to reach any one of these goals, says Brown, is likely to mean a failure to achieve the others as well. Brown talks to Sonu Jain about his book, the global social tipping point and why he would be worried about his future if he were living in India.

•What is the most important difference between the last Plan B 2:0 and this version?

The first one was released five or six years ago. In this, there is a sense of urgency. Earlier we talked about saving the planet. Now it is about saving civilisation. So many structures keeping the world together are falling apart: There is a tightening of food supplies and rising oil prices, leading to instability and unrest particularly in middle income countries. We are seeing a peak oil situation. It means that no country gets more oil without another losing some. I call it APO (after peak oil) and BPO (before peak oil): These are two distinct eras in history.

•What are the new facts that support your theory of the world falling apart in your latest book?

We need not go beyond ice melting to see that civilisation is in trouble. Business as usual is no longer a viable option. It is time for Plan B. If Antarica ice melts, the sea level will go up by 7 metres and Bangladesh will lose 40 per cent of its rice land. Scientists have told us that the glaciers of the Himalayan and the Tibetan plateau are shrinking at an accelerated rate.
