Resuming on 235 for three, Shivnarine Chanderpaul and Dwayne Bravo hit confident half centuries but their dismissal just before the lunch allowed Australia to sniff victory. West Indies, chasing an improbable 475 to win, stretched their overnight 235 for three to 316 for five at lunch. Left-hander Chanderpaul hit an even 50 and added 122 with the effervescent Bravo, who cracked 69.

But left-arm wrist spinner Beau Casson (two for 80) and pacer Stuart Clark (two for 40) made the crucial breakthroughs 20 minutes before the break. Chanderpaul and Bravo began cautiously against the accurate Clark and the left-arm spin of Michael Clarke and added 33 runs in the first hour.

The introduction of paceman Brett Lee tested the home side. But Bravo brought up his 50 off 113 balls, and then blossomed against Casson with three huge sixes over long-off. Chanderpaul notched up 8,000 runs when he reached 49, the fourth West Indian to do so after Brian Lara (11,953), Sir Vivian Richards (8,540) and Sir Garfield Sobers (8,032).

Casson dismissed Bravo, who prodded forward defensively and gave a catch to Phil Jaques at short leg. Bravo lashed five fours and four sixes off 133 balls.

Australia took the second new ball in the next over and Clark trapped Chanderpaul leg before to silence the crowd. It was the first time Australia had dismissed the slim left-hander in the series.

Australia were fired up by the double breakthrough and Jerome Taylor (7 not out) and Denesh Ramdin (0 not out) survived a torrid 15-minute burst from Lee and Clark before lunch. After lunch, Taylor made a spirited 31, his highest score in Tests and injured Sewnarine Chattergoon hobbled out with a runner to keep the chase alive. But Mitchell Johnson soon got Taylor caught behind and Brett Lee did the same for Chattergoon.

Brief Scores: Australia 251 & 439/5 decl beat West Indies 216 & 387 (X Marshall 85, D Bravo 69, Chanderpaul 50, R Sarwan 43, Clark 3/58, Casson 3/86, Lee 2/109) by 87 runs.

Heading: How Bollywood’s famous villain inspired a cricket hero - Indian Express
Content:
On the day a Mumbai court adjourned the Rs 29 million misappropriation case against former ICC president Jagmohan Dalmiya, there were whispers in Kolkata about his re-entry into cricket.

Speaking to The Indian Express this evening, former CAB assistant secretary and a staunch Dalmiya aide, Biswarup Dey, said: "Now it's confirmed that Dalmiya is contesting the CAB elections. We are all rallying behind him, and if he contests for the CAB president's post, he is bound to get a clear majority in the 121-vote pie."

Although the court's decision comes as a relief for Dalmiya, the former CAB and BCCI president maintained that the case was never an obstacle for him to contest the election.

"That was a regular course of hearing. The hurdle was never there. If you have any information that the court ruling was any a roadblock (in contesting CAB polls), it's false and fictitious," Dalmiya told a news agency shortly after the court's verdict to defer the case. Dalmiya was at the helm of the CAB for 13 years before he lost a high-voltage election to Prasun Mukherjee. Dalmiya-aide Dey will contest for the CAB joint-secretary's post in the July-end elections.

Heading: AIIMS forensic team doctor questions ‘key’ entry in Arushi’s post mortem report - Indian Express
Content:
The hero of India's historic World Cup triumph in 1983, Mohinder Amarnath, admits he was nervous before the final - but drew inspiration from the Bollywood blockbuster Sholay to get over the jitters of playing against two-time champions West Indies in the title clash.

"I remembered the famous dialogue of Sholay — jo dar gaya so mar gaya. I told myself that it was my day and I had nothing to lose," said Amarnath, who was adjudged Man of the Match in both the semi-final and the final.

Twenty-five years after the historic triumph, Amarnath described the Indian dressing room's atmosphere before the big match as calm and said the underdogs were in high spirits.

"We were very relaxed on the day of the final. Not a single player panicked. We were playing together for quiet some time, hence there was mutual understanding and confidence of winning," the all-rounder said.

In the final played at Lord's, Amarnath scored 26 runs and took three important wickets for just 12 runs in seven overs as the West Indies team collapsed on 140 chasing a 183-run target. Amarnath said neither did he fear the dangerous pace trio of Joel Garner, Michel Holding and Andy Roberts, nor was he intimidated by explosive batsman Vivian Richards.

Dream come true

Amarnath, who played 69 Tests and 85 ODIs for India, said the triumph was something out of the world for the Indians and seemed like a dream. "We used to watch World Cup finals sitting beyond the boundary line. It was a dream to play a final and hold the trophy. We literally lived that dream on June 25, 1983," Amarnath said.

"It has been 25 years since then but I can still feel the thrill as if we have just won yesterday. It was an unexpected win and we are proud of it," he added.

Amarnath said that despite the odds, the Indians were determined to win as it was a once in a lifetime opportunity to be at the top. "All of us were determined to win. You have to be numero uno as nobody remembers the runner-up," he said.

Turning point

He rated his Man of the Match award in that game as the biggest achievement of his life. "Definitely, it is my most precious asset. Things were going right for me before the World Cup but that win changed everything.

"It was one of the rare opportunities when the whole nation celebrated together. There was no bar of religion, age, language or class. We have given a reason to smile to every Indian and that was the most memorable part of the win," he recalled.

Heading: Look what China’s up to, we need own space command: Army chief - Indian Express
Content:
A month after 14-year-old Arushi Talwar was murdered, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), which took over the case a fortnight ago, isn't the only one questioning the investigation of the Noida police.

Now experts at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), who are working closely with the CBI, have raised questions over one entry in Arushi's post mortem report.

The report, dated May 16 and prepared by Sunil Dore for the Noida police, mentions "whitish discharge" from the vagina which AIIMS doctors say wasn't investigated. They have raised this issue with the CBI.

"It is the duty of the doctors and the investigating officer to collect all biological evidence. As per law, it is mandatory to write about it in the post mortem report which is legal evidence. But in this case no further investigation was done on the evidence that they got from natural orifices," Sudhir Gupta, associate professor, forensic medicine, AIIMS, told The Indian Express. Gupta is one of the doctors in the team scrutinising the post mortem report.

The post mortem report says that various organs including stomach with contents, samples from small intestine, gall bladder, spleen and one kidney were preserved, sealed and sent for examination to rule out poisoning.

"However, the report doesn't mention whether a vaginal swab was sent for further investigation," said Gupta. "The whitish discharge could be attributed to several causes, from a fungal infection, common at this age, to even sexual assault. But in a murder case, this was a serious biological finding which required deliberation. No such type of biological evidence was collected and sealed by the doctor who prepared the autopsy," he added.

Contacted by The Indian Express, Dore said: "Investigation (of the discharge) was done but I cannot disclose the findings...If I have not mentioned it in the report, that means there was nothing of that sort (sexual assault)."

According to the post mortem report, AIIMS doctors said, the first blow on Arushi's head was sufficient to cause her death but she could have remained alive for at least 10 minutes to half an hour, after which her neck was slit. This incision measured 14 cm X 6 cm above the thyroid cartilage.

Heading: To guard satellites, India plans monitoring facility - Indian Express
Content:
A month after Navy Chief Sureesh Mehta expressed concern over the growing fleet of Chinese nuclear submarines, Army chief General Deepak Kapoor has pointed at the "exponentially fast pace" with which China is developing its space programme for military purposes.

In a rare comment on the Indian space programme, the Army chief, issuing a veiled warning on the rapid growth of Chinese space capabilities, emphasised the urgency of establishing a joint Space Command.

"Chinese space programme is expanding at an exponentially rapid pace in both offensive and defensive content... There is an attempt to try and militarise space. There are also agreements that space militarisation should be restricted," General Kapoor said. He was speaking at a seminar on Space Applications for Military Use organised by defence think tank Centre for Land Warfare Studies (CLAWS).

The General's frank assessment of the Chinese programme comes just a week after the Defence Ministry announced the creation of an Integrated Space Cell to counter the "growing threat" to space assets in the wake of "offensive anti-satellite weaponry" in the neighbourhood.

Kapoor's statement comes a month after the Navy chief commented on the new Chinese nuclear base in Hainan Island and said that the growing number of nuclear submarines in the region is a cause for concern.

Asserting that it is the Army's endeavour to "optimize space applications for military purposes", General Kapoor said that the establishment of a tri-services space command for "persistent surveillance and rapid response" is an urgent requirement.

"Military usage of space in the Indian context is at a comparatively nascent stage...There is an imperative requirement to develop joint structures for synergizing employment of space assets," he said.

While the Indian military establishment has been talking about the urgency of setting up space assets, the Army has for the first time come out openly for the immediate "exploitation of space" for military use.

"With time, we will get sucked into a military race to protect our space assets and inevitably there will be a military contest in space. In a life and death scenario, space will provide the advantage," said Lt Gen H S Lidder, chief of the Integrated Defence Staff under which the Space Cell has been established.

Heading: Indian in Spanish jail on terror charges will  finally get day in court - Indian Express
Content:
India is planning to set up a monitoring facility to protect its space assets against threats from Anti Satellite (ASAT) weapon systems like the one tested by China in January last year.

The new facility, conceptualized after the Chinese test brought out the vulnerability of Indian space systems, will consist of a geostationary satellite and a ground station that will detect threats to space assets. This will enable the ground controller to steer away the threatened satellite to safety, a top ISRO scientist said.

While India has always been uncomfortable with the Chinese ASAT test that brought down an obsolete weather satellite, this is the first time that visible steps have been taken to counter the new threat. The timeline of the project has not been shared but it is expected to be merged when a tri-Services Space Command is set up.

The monitoring facility, designed to observe and warn satellites about incoming threats, will also have jamming systems to counter ASAT systems. "We are planning to first put up a geostationary satellite in orbit to monitor any object that is coming close to our satellites.

If there is a threat, the satellite would be shifted slightly to a safer place," said Geeta Vardhan, Programme Director (Special Projects), ISRO, speaking at a session on Space Applications for Military Use in India.

Vardhan said that the system is still in a developmental stage but would consist of a geostationary satellite with sensors that would monitor movements in space. A communication satellite would be used to transmit signals to a ground station where controllers would be able to make minor adjustments to the satellite path to veer it out of danger's way.

Besides the military self-defence application, the facility will also serve as a warning system against space debris than can destroy satellites. "There is increasing number of debris in space and we will need to know whether they are heading towards a satellite," Vardhan said.

While India remains committed to non-weaponization of space, Defence Minister A K Antony hinted at a more aggressive approach last week by saying that an integrated space cell is required due to the presence of counter space systems in the neighbourhood.

Heading: Tech trumps tradition, players get to challenge umpires, thrice each innings - Indian Express
Content:
Five months after he was arrested by Spanish authorities in a suspected terror plot, Mumbai-resident Roshan Jamal Khan is set to be produced in court for the first time this week and his lawyers plan to seek his release on bail.

Khan was among 14 Muslim men picked up from a mosque in Barcelona on January 19 and Spanish police allege they were planning to set off bombs in that city. Four of them, including another Indian, were released later. Khan, who is being held along with nine Pakistanis, was in Spain to explore the possibility of starting an olives business, his family has said.

"He was brought to Madrid about a week ago and his lawyers have received letters saying the 10 men will be produced in court on June 17 and 18," Khan's brother-in-law, Amanullah Khan, told The Indian Express from Barcelona. "We still don't know if he has been personally charged of anything but the lawyers have been told that he faces the same allegations as the others in the group."

It was not clear if all 10 suspects would be produced together or separately and their lawyers would seek bail saying the men could be released while the police conduct their investigations, he said. Khan's family is hoping for a positive turn of events as the Spanish Consulate in Mumbai had late last month written to his wife assuring that her husband would be treated fairly by Spanish law.

The family had been worried by the death last month of Khan's lawyer Sebastian Sallelas but Amanullah said that Sallelas' son was handling the case as part of a group of 10 lawyers representing the suspects and about five of those lawyers were expected to be in court.

In the letter dated May 29 to Khan's wife Farida, the Consul-General of Spain in Mumbai, Cesar Alba, had said that her husband was detained under operation 'Cantata', that was launched by the Civil Guard. 'Cantata' roughly translates as "singing", a term often used by police to describe an informant spilling the beans on his accomplices. "Mr. Khan is in prison awaiting judgement for a crime of integrating with a terrorist organisation and of illegal possession of explosives," the diplomat had said.

Heading: Rajdhanis, Shatabdis ‘popular’ trains, so fare cut is cut - Indian Express
Content:
With Sachin Tendulkar just 171 runs short of Brian Lara's highest Test run-getter record, next month's India versus Sri Lanka series had the potential to be part of cricketing history. But much before Tendulkar takes guard in the first Test in Colombo on July 23, the series was guaranteed a special mention in the annals of the game today.

For the first time, the series will see players being allowed to appeal against an umpire's decision. The new system, that increases the use of TV replays and advanced technology in the game and was recommended by ICC's cricket committee in March earlier this year, will be on trial during the series. BCCI secretary Niranjan Shah said that the two boards had mutually agreed to be part of this ICC experiment.

Each team will be permitted to question the umpire three times in an innings. A failed appeal will cost the team one challenge, whereas the team will get an additional appeal if the review results in a reversal of the umpire's decision. The rule will apply, as per a BCCI statement, to all modes of dismissal except 'Timed Out' where a batsman is given out for taking too long to reach the crease.

On appeal, the umpire's decision will be referred to the third umpire, who will then be allowed to use slow-motion replays, stump microphones and Hawk-Eye technology to analyse the decision. However, Hawk-Eye will be used only for ball-tracking purposes and not, as it is on television coverage, to estimate the future trajectory of the ball.

According to elite panel umpire A V Jayaprakash, this limited use of Hawk-Eye will keep the most debatable mode of dismissal, leg before wicket, still in limbo. "Since Hawk Eye's estimate of the future trajectory of the ball wouldn't be taken into consideration, the debate over LBW cannot be stopped," he said.

The referral request by the player can be made by making a 'T' sign with both forearms at head height. He should then indicate 'out' by raising his finger or indicate 'not out' by crossing his hands three times.

Heading: Arrests shatter myth only Muslims behind blasts: CM - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: SC provides legal aid for Gujarat riots probe team - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra Police on Tuesday arrested two more members of a little-known radical Hindu group in connection with the crude bomb blasts at theatres screening a controversial Marathi play, close on the heels of Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh saying the arrests in the case had blown a hole in the popular perception that Muslims are to be suspected for all such attacks.

The two men arrested on Tuesday were members of the Sanatan Sanstha while the two held on Monday were members of the Sanstha as well as that of the Hindu Janajagruti Samiti (HJS). They have been accused of planting bombs in two auditoriums in Navi Mumbai and Thane two weeks ago and for one which went off during the screening of Bollywood film Jodhaa Akbar, also in Navi Mumbai, in February.

Only two of the three bombs — crude, low-intensity devices —exploded and injured a handful of people. The two organisations have been quick to disown the men, saying they were acting on their own even though the HJS has been vocal about its opposition to the Marathi play, Amhi Pachpute, saying it insults Hindu mythologicals.

But the arrests were enough for Deshmukh to point fingers at the possibility of Hindu groups being involved in subversive activities too. "Normally, when such incidents take place a particular community is suspected," the Chief Minister said in a statement late on Monday. "But the arrest of two people belonging to a Hindu organisation proves that such suspicions are baseless. Criminals don't belong to any religion."

Although the HJS and the Sanatan Sanstha have vociferously proclaimed their innocence, the arrests have brought back memories of April 2006 when two people were killed in a blast in the house of prominent RSS activist in Maharashtra's Nanded town. Those men were believed to be members of Bajrang Dal according to Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) investigators and the ATS suspects Sanatan Sanstha and HJS may have links with or worked in the past with the Bajrang Dal. This week's arrests, they say, have thrown the spotlight on what are apparently shadowy organisations that have largely been operating in the hinterlands of Maharashtra and fuelling right wing extremism.

HJS national spokesperson Dr Durgesh Samant was agitated when asked if his group was a "Hindu terror" organisation as investigators suspected. "We are not just a Hindu nationalist organisation. We also take up nationalissues. All these allegations that we are a saffron group are incorrect and have been created by miscreants," he told The Indian Express from Goa where HJS is registered.

On the other hand, the Sanatan Sanstha, set up in 1999, has an ashram in Sukhapur village near Panvel, about 50 km from Mumbai. Over the past week, the ashram on the banks of the Gadhi river saw several police teams visiting to question the sevaks and the management. "The allegations against us are false," said Abhay Vartak, the spokesperson for the ashram. "In fact, we condemn such incidents and this is not the way of protesting."

Those at the ashram recollect Ramesh Gadkari, arrested for planting the bomb that exploded in Thane's Gadkari auditorium, as a quiet man living in the ashram with his wife for five years. "They did menial jobs. He mostly looked after construction activities. He attended satsang only once a week," said Vartak.

Through its newspaper Sanatan Prabhat, the ashram has condemned the blast with an editorial that said, "Though we condemn the act, the mindset and the anger of these (arrested) people should be understood and the mocking of Hindu gods should be stopped."

Hindu Janajagruti Samiti

The organisation which is "uniting Hindus globally" has no headquarters or formal membership, but has a strong online presence. It owes its genesis to an October 2002 meeting where Hindu deities were "blasphemously criticised" and a solitary man who protested was attacked. "With a view to protest against this attack, all Hindu organisations came together and the Hindu Janajagruti Samiti was established on the 13th October 2002 by initiative of seekers of Sanatan Sanstha," says the outift's website. At present, the group's global agenda is to protest the "anti-Hindu" Hollywood movie The Love Guru, "anti-Hindu textbooks" for schoolchildren in Goa and saving the Ram Sethu.

Heading: Naxals storm marriage function, kill bridegroom - Indian Express
Content:
Following a request by former CBI director R K Raghavan, chief of the Special Investigative Team (SIT) formed to carry out a fresh probe into 10 cases of the 2002 Gujarat riots, the Supreme Court on Tuesday asked Solicitor General G E Vahanavti and another senior advocate to assist the team.

A Vacation Bench presided over by Justice Arijit Pasayat asked Vahanavti and K G Menon, another senior advocate, to provide all sorts of legal help to the SIT in conducting their probe.

Earlier in March, a three-member Bench, also presided over by Justice Pasayat had ordered the Modi Government to set up a SIT which would take a fresh look into some of the worst riots cases of 2002. The SIT includes three senior police officers from Gujarat — Gita Johri, Sivananad Jha and Ashish Bhatia. It also has former Uttar Pradesh DGP C B Satpathy.

Asked to submit its report within three months, the SIT will probe 10 cases relating to rioting in seven places. This includes Godhra where 81 people were killed and the Gulbarga Society where 68 were massacred.

Heading: Biometric passports from next year: Pranab - Indian Express
Content:
Naxalites stormed a marriage function and killed the bridegroom by slitting his throat before the guests at Koder village in Maoist infested Bijapur district on Monday night.

The extremists fled from the scene after killing Laxman Parlipal, who used to assist security forces at the Cherpal relief camp.

Meanwhile, CRPF personnel and Maoist rebels had a two-hour long encounter near Kondagaon in Kanker district on Tuesday afternoon. The paramilitary forces were attacked by the rebels on their way to a nearby village following information that the Naxalites had killed a trader.

Police said CRPF head constable Devidas was killed in the encounter while another head constable Shatrughan Singh Yadav and constable Grijashankar sustained serious injuries. Both the injured were rushed to Kanker district hospital.

Two CRPF platoons had moved to Kondagaon to recover the body of Rakesh Kumar Singh, a trader who was abducted by the rebels on June 14, along with his two brothers. The rebels let off two of them, but killed Rakesh and left his body near Kondagaon.

In another incident, Naxalites set ablaze an earth moving machine engaged in road construction at Lakshmipura under Pakhanjur police station in Kanker district.

Heading: Over four lakh people affected by Assam floods - Indian Express
Content:
The Government will launch electronic passports and simplify their issuance procedure from next year, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee said on Tuesday. He was inaugurating the first passport office of Uttarakhand here along with Chief Minister B C Khanduri.

E-passports will carry the prescribed biological features and facial imprints of a holder and will be at par with international standards. Mukherjee said the Government plans to make use of service providers for the issuing of passports, adding that 68 centres have already been set up across India. "The process of selection of the service providers is in its final stage. The police verification will also be expedited through electronic devices," he added.

The Passport Seva Project is expected to be completed in 19 months. Under this project, passports will be issued within three days and those applying for a Tatkal passport will get it within a day of submission of forms.

Heading: NCP, UDP may put up common candidate for parliamentary polls - Indian Express
Content:
The flood situation in Assam continued to be grim, with the Brahmaputra and several of its tributaries flowing above the danger level. As the toll in the flash floods that hit Lakhimpur district on Saturday reached 21, Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi flew to the affected areas, directing the civil authorities to provide relief to the people.

With fresh areas getting inundated in Lakhimpur and adjoining Dhemaji district in eastern Assam, the total number of people affected has been put at over four lakh. The district authorities have so far accommodated about 25,000 persons in 14 relief camps, while over one lakh people are still living in non-official camps without any relief from the Government. As many as 50 villages in Telahi tehsil in Lakhimpur were inundated on Tuesday, affecting over 1,000 families.

Gogoi, who visited the spot near Lakhimpur where National Highway 52 was cut off by the flood waters, has requested the Army to immediately construct a bailey bridge in order to restore communication to Lakhimpur and Dhemaji districts. The two districts in eastern Assam along with several districts in Arunachal Pradesh have remained cut off since Saturday.

The authorities have shifted 400 families to safer places after the Dikrong, a tributary of the Brahmaputra flowing down from Arunachal Pradesh, threatened to breach an embankment that has been protecting the Bihpuria town in Lakhimpur.

Heading: ‘Army killed cadres in fake encounters’ - Indian Express
Content:
The NCP-United Democratic Party-led Meghalaya Progressive Alliance (MPA) has decided to put up a common candidate for the Shillong Lok Sabha seat in the 2009 Parliamentary elections.

Former Lok Sabha speaker and NCP general secretary Purno A Sangma said on Tuesday: "We are in discussions with the UDP for finding a consensus candidate for the Shillong seat for the the Lok Sabha elections."

In its executive committee meeting held on Tuesday, the NCP rued its inability to make a significant foray into the Khasi and Jaintia Hills districts of Meghalaya in the March 3 State election—it only managed to pick up two seat— and won the rest of its 13 seats from the Garo Hills district.

However, it hopes to alter the situation in the 2009 District Councils and Parliamentary elections. After the committee meeting on Tuesday, NCP state secretary and Deputy Chief Minister Timothy D Shira said that the party has urged its workers to pull up their socks and to start preparing for the elections.

According to Shira, many party leaders felt that the NCP's poor performance in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills was because it was perceived to be Garo Hills-based party.

"There were rumours spread by rivals that the NCP is neither a national nor regional but a Garo party. We didn't counter that effectively," he admitted.

However, as far as vote share is concerned, the NCP is satisfied with the number of votes that it got in the 2008 Assembly election. Shira said that the party had won only 43,000 votes in 2003, but had doubled its vote share to 87,000 in 2008.

"We are happy that the NCP has increased its votes share in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills, but the party candidates must work hard for the coming elections," said Shira.

Heading: Meghalaya lobbies for Phrang Roy as India’s nominee for IFAD president - Indian Express
Content:
United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) peace broker and People's Consultative Group (PCG) member Hiranya Saikia on Tuesday accused the Army of killing cadres in fake encounters. The Army had earlier claimed that in recent months security forces had killed 68 rebels.

"The ULFA has not touched a single security personnel. Neither has it resorted to any kind of violence, on the expectation that the Government would send some positive signals. But what the Government has done is to gun down ULFA cadres through false encounters," Saikia, considered a close confidante of ULFA chief Paresh Barua, has said.

The PCG member accused the Army and security forces of large-scale violation of human rights and said in most cases the Army had killed the cadres instead of handing them over to the police. "The Army has sweeping rights to kill anybody just on suspicion under provisions of the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act. This is flagrant violation of human rights," Saikia said. The Army has killed 15 cadres in 10 days, he added.

Saikia referred to Sunday's incident at Kanubari-Balijan Grant in Sivasagar district where three hardcore ULFA rebels, Badal Khargharia alias Bigyan Konwar, Basa Bauri and Nitul Rajkonwar alias Sonit Gohain, were killed.

"The three were killed in cold blood but the Army later claimed that they were killed in a fierce encounter. There is strong evidence that the three boys were killed after they were apprehended from a house," Saikia said.

Since January, 68 rebels were killed and 60 have been apprehended and handed over to the police.

Over 180 ULFA activists have surrendered. A large number of weapons, including several AK-series rifles, UMGs and other sophisticated arms and ammunition, have been recovered from them.

Heading: Amarnath yatra kicks off, board says all in place - Indian Express
Content:
The Meghalaya Progressive Alliance (MPA) coalition Government is pushing hard for the nomination of Meghalaya's Phrang Roy as India's candidate for the post of president of the International Federation of Agriculture Development (IFAD). Roy has already served as the vice-president of the organisation and many here feel that if the Central Government nominates him, he will stand a good chance of clinching the IFAD's top post

MPA chief architect and chairman of the Meghalaya State Planning Board (SPB), Purno A Sangma, is also lobbying Roy's candidature by requesting support from chief ministers of other northeastern states.

Sangma said on Monday: "I will be going to Guwahati to garner support for Roy, so that we can speak to the Centre in unison for his candidature. Sangma has also written a letter to Union Finance Minister P Chidambaram to consider Roy as India's nominee. However, as the election for the IFAD president is slated for April 2009, Chidambaram has told Sangma that it is currently too early to assess India's chances of getting its candidate elected to the post."

Heading: Forces within and outside may disrupt J-K polls: Antony - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Amarnath Yatra began on Tuesday with the first batch of 2,837 pilgrims starting their journey from Jammu to the cave shrine in South Kashmir, the organisers of the yatra, Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB), said they were fully geared for the holy pilgrimage.

"All the agencies concerned are working in tandem to make the yatra successful," Principal Secretary to Governor and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of SASB Arun Kumar said in Srinagar, adding elaborate arrangements were in place for making it an incident-free yatra.

Regretting the controversies over the pilgrimage, Kumar said all modern scientific measures had been taken to ensure that no harm was caused to the environment.

"Let me make it clear that SASB is not raising any permanent structures anywhere in the base camp or en route the cave shrine. The pre-fabricated huts have been installed as these can withstand weather vagaries," he said. "We are aware of the environmental concerns. But if people still want that the yatra route or base camp should be like Switzerland then we need to construct permanent structures."

He said the board was still of the opinion that an independent Amarnath Development Authority (ADA) should be constituted for the smooth handling of the pilgrimage. Jammu and Kashmir Governor Lt Gen S K Sinha, who also heads the SASB, had recently written a letter to Deputy Chief Minister Muzaffar Hussain Beig for constituting an ADA. However, the state Government turned down the proposal.

"When we have development bodies for Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Sonamarg and many other places, what is wrong with Amarnath Developmental Authority?" he asked.

Early in the morning, the yatra began amid slogans of "Jai Bholey Baba, Jai Baba Amarnath" and tight security, with a three-tier security ring of over 6,000 CRPF personnel deployed along the route from Jammu to Pahalgam.

The convoy of 59 buses carrying the pilgrims, escorted by vehicles carrying CRPF personnel, was flagged off by J&K Minister for Higher Education G S Charak at around 5 am.

They will have darshan at the cave shrine on Wednesday. The 2,837 yatris comprised 1,846 men, 778 women, 174 children and 67 sadhus.

Assistant Commissioner Revenue Rajinder Singh, who is the nodal officer for the Amarnath yatra in Jammu, said that the Government had tried to provide all kinds of facilities to ensure a safe and comfortable journey for the pilgrims.

Heading: AMU security upgradation: body wants Arjun’s intervention - Indian Express
Content:
Apprehending trouble from forces "within and outside Jammu and Kashmir", Defence Minister A K Antony on Tuesday asked security forces and government officials to make all-out efforts to ensure peaceful elections in the state scheduled later this year.

"The coming months are going to be crucial as there are forces within and outside the state which will make efforts to thwart the process of holding elections in the state," Antony told a meeting of top security and state government officials here.

In the meeting, attended by J-K Chief Minister Ghulam Nabi Azad and senior military officials, Antony was briefed about the overall security situation of the state and arrangements made for the peaceful commencement of the Amarnath Yatra that began on Tuesday.

While complimenting the security forces for bringing down the level of militancy-related violence in the state, Antony asked the security forces to vacate all remaining public buildings and ensure that human rights was not violated in the process.

"Security forces alone cannot provide lasting peace, stability and prosperity. For this, the people have to realise that peace alone pays dividends," Antony said, adding that the Centre will provide all support to make J-K one of the frontline states in development.

Antony will be visiting forward posts on the Line of Control in Uri on Wednesday.

Heading: Nod for rail link between new Bangalore airport, city - Indian Express
Content:
The Human Resource Development Ministry will look into the proposed security upgrade mooted for the Aligarh Muslim University. The issue has become a bone of contention between Vice-Chancellor P K Abdul Azis and the executive council. On Tuesday, some members of the council submitted a memorandum to

Union HRD Minister Arjun Singh, terming the proposed measures as excessive and unnecessary. They sought the ministry's intervention in the matter.

AMU has invited tenders for deployment of 433 security personnel, including 37 gunmen, 30 CCTVs, 50 walkie-talkie sets, metal detectors, one X-ray scanner, smoke detectors, among other things.

The high security measures were proposed after AMU had to close down for two months last year soon after the murder of a second-year engineering student, followed by violence in the university. AMU had then demanded paramilitary deployment to control the situation.

Some members of the executive council have objected to the proposed security measures, arguing that the "paraphernalia seems to be more than adequate for a high security defence establishment; why buy them for an educational institution like AMU?". The members also said that the proposed measures do not have the approval of the executive council.

Heading: Ramdev meets Ramadoss - Indian Express
Content:
Following up on a clearance provided earlier this year by the dispensation under the Governor, the new Government in the state has also accorded its approval for a high-speed rail link between the new Bengaluru International Airport and the city.

The Rs 3,561 crore rail link project, prepared with the technical expertise of the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation and first cleared in December 2007, has received the Government's approval, Chief Minister B S Yeddyurappa announced on Tuesday following a review of infrastructure projects for the city. The rail link would enable commuters to cover a distance of 33 km between the city and the new airport in 25 minutes, against the current minimum of 45 to 60 minutes. Yeddyurappa reiterated plans to have check-in counters for the new airport on Cubbon Road at the starting point of the rail link facility.

A special purpose vehicle to implement the project, featuring the state Government, DMRC, and Bangalore International Airport Limited, has already been created. State Government officials on Tuesday said that the rail link would be established under public-private-partnership model.

The Government also announced plans to buy 310 Volvo buses for Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation to ply as a high-end service in the city. A limited Volvo bus service already exists with the BMTC.

In another key push for a pending project, reviewed by the CM, the Bangalore Development Authority has decided to float a global tender for building the first phase of 65 km of a 115 km peripheral ring road around the city.

For the Rs 3,000 crore road, intended to decongest traffic within Bangalore, around 1,800 acres of land has already been acquired, officials said.

The BDA has also announced plans to build 92,000 small flats, costing around Rs 3 lakh each for the economically weaker section.

"It is my dream to transform Bangalore into a global city in the real sense of the term. In our manifesto, we have come out with a blueprint for this purpose. We intend to provide infrastructure that can match global standards," Yeddyurappa said on Tuesday.

A delegation of MPs from the state would meet Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Finance Minister P Chidambaram for clearance of pending projects for Bangalore, he added.

Yeddyurappa also announced the convening of a meeting at the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, on June 28 where suggestions for improvement of city's infrastructure would be sought from industrialists, NGOs, opinion-makers and experts.

Heading: Another row, more poll fodder - Indian Express
Content:
Yoga guru Baba Ramdev called on Health Minister Ramadoss on Tuesday, taking forward their newfound camaraderie and their joint mission to combat harmful substances such as alcohol, tobacco and even junk food.

According to sources, the visit at Ramadoss's residence lasted a good half hour, with both parties commending each other's efforts in promoting good health. "They discussed the health benefits of yoga and also that it should be introduced to rural areas. Both the minister and Baba Ramdev were quite agreeable towards a new co-operation," said an official.

Their newly forged cooperation, however, is a drastic turnaround from last year when the two engaged in a war of words over the treatment of AIDS. While Baba Ramdev had claimed that yoga could prove to be a cure for the disease, the Health Minister retaliated by questioning the scientific validity of the yoga guru's claims.

Heading: BJP has an image problem - Indian Express
Content:
After the Amarnath Shrine Board controversy, the J&K Government is facing another serious crisis involving the functioning of the state-run Waqf Council—a body that manages Muslim shrines, graveyards and other properties in Jammu.

The state government has admitted that its various departments, the J&K Police, Army and civilian encroachers have illegally occupied 3,144 kanals of waqf land, including graveyards. In fact, the Waqf Council that is headed by Chief Minister Ghulam Nabi Azad—he is in charge of the Hajj and Auqaf ministry—has prepared the list of its encroached properties which includes a shrine and a Jamia mosque.

The records of the Hajj and Auqaf ministry clearly indicate that the government had taken up the cases of waqf encroachment in Jammu seriously in 2006. In fact, the minutes of a meeting held by the then Principal Secretary, Revenue and Hajj and Auqaf, reveal that the government has been aware of the scale of these encroachments across Jammu, majority of it carried out by the government's own departments like Education, Health, Rural Development, Public Works and Police. The minutes of the meeting also reveal that the government had issued directions to the encroachers, asking them to vacate the Jamia Mosque at RS Pora and return it to the Waqf. However, there has been no serious headway in these encroachment cases ever since.

Why has the issue of Waqf land encroachment come up now? The reason is that the assembly elections are just four months away. The latest controversy was triggered by outgoing Governor S.K. Sinha's letter to the state government demanding the establishment of an independent development authority controlled by the Amarnath Shrine Board. Subsequently, the Azad government's decision to transfer forestland to the Board turned it into another major controversy here.

Political parties have started exploiting this situation. Chief Minister Azad is silent over the Amarnath land transfer issue while his coalition ally, the Peoples Democratic Party, has openly accused the Congress of blackmailing their ministers and forcing them to accept the controversial land transfer.

The Amarnath Shrine Board, meanwhile, has become an emotive issue in the Hindu-dominated districts of Jammu where both the Congress and its archrival, the BJP, are trying to exhibit their Jammu-centric credentials by supporting the Shrine Board as well as Raj Bhawan. This story, in fact, goes back to 2004 when the state government opposed Raj Bhawan's plan to extend the yatra to two months. Then chief minister Mufti Mohammad Sayeed had turned down the Raj Bhawan proposal which soon turned into a major political crisis with four Congress ministers from Jammu resigning from the government. The issue has, in fact, polarised the J&K Congress party and while the Congress leadership from Jammu supported the Raj Bhawan, its Kashmir-based leadership preferred to remain silent.

The opposition National Conference—which was responsible for bringing the legislation empowering Raj Bhawan to run the Shrine Board in 2001—has been trying to distance itself from its earlier decision. This is because the party is trying to regain its traditional base in Kashmir, where the PDP has come up as their serious competitor since the 2002 assembly polls.

In fact, this controversy suits the vote-bank politics of both the Congress and the PDP. The Congress banks on Jammu votes and is expecting to gain in the Hindu-dominated province. Now the controversy over the Waqf Council will provide fodder for mainstream political parties in their poll campaigns.

The separatists too are uniting because these two issues—Amarnath land transfer in Kashmir and Waqf property encroachments in Jammu—have provided them a chance and an emotive subject to revive their base across Kashmir.

Politics and pilgrimage

2000: J&K State Legislative assembly passed Shri Amarnath Shrine Board Act, making the Governor the chairman of the board. Till then, the shrine was administered by the Prohit Sabha, and the Mattan and Dashnami Akhara.

2004: J-K Government and Raj Bhawan differed on duration of Amarnath yatra. The Governor wanted the yatra to be extended to two months from the traditional month-long annual pilgrimage. Then Chief minister, PDP's Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, refused, citing additional burden on security. The issue assumed a communal dimension as four Congress ministers from Jammu resigned.

2005: Shrine Board decided to bring in commercial helicopter service to ferry pilgrims to Amarnath. J-K Tourism Corporation insisted on using state helicopters but the shrine board termed it interference in its work. The issue was settled in the High Court.

2007: A top PDP minister refused to let the Board construct a motorable road from Baltal to Amarnath, citing "disastrous environmental implications".

2008: State government rejected a report of an advisory committee which had recommended transfer of land in Baltal to Shri Amarnath Shrine Board for construction of road and raising hutments at various points.

Heading: Round 1 of cable war goes to Marans - Indian Express
Content:
While the ruling BJP is desperately trying to improve its image by doling out pro-poor sops, a series of developments has left it red in the face, something it could have done without in an election year.

A $2500 donation from Dow Chemicals, the US-based company that acquired Union Carbide a few years ago, is the latest. The amount is not significant but it has given the Opposition an opportunity to accuse the party of taking money from a company the gas tragedy victims were trying to bring to justice.

This was preceded by an embarrassing incident of a minister caught stealing power for nearly eight years. By some strange coincidence, the theft came to light when the chief minister was announcing his government's decision to withdraw cases of power thefts against farmers. Ramdayal Ahirwar, who was recently inducted as minister of state for home, did not have a valid electricity connection at his home in Chhatarpur district. The veteran leader was forced to apply for a proper connection once the matter became public.

It all began when the minister's son beat up a policeman and vandalised his house. Laxmi Ahirwar, a Nagar Panchayat president, was angry because the cop had refused to arrange for vehicles to welcome the minister. A power failure a few days later angered the minister's son and he thrashed the cop when he refused to restore electricity. It did not take long for the public to know that the minister did not have a valid power connection.

Ajay Vishnoi's resignation after the Income Tax department raids on the properties of his brother and of other health department officials is the latest embarrassment for the BJP government. The raids had revealed how corrupt officials in the health department colluded with suppliers and manufacturers to siphon off money meant for schemes in rural areas. The department deals with grants—running into hundreds of crores—from the central government and international funding agencies.

The IT raids had followed similar action against then director of medical services, Dr Yogiraj Sharma, and his associates last year. As the IT sleuths pieced together details of properties amassed by Sharma and his accomplices, it turned out that the racket was in excess of Rs 100 crore.

While Sharma was allowed to escape with a minor punishment—he was asked to take compulsory retirement—the government did little to punish others as irregularities continued without any check. Vishnoi refused to quit, arguing his premises were not raided, but the party high command forced to him to resign.

Emboldened by Vishnoi's resignation, the Opposition came out with a list of ministers who are facing corruption charges and cases against whom are pending with the Lokayukta. With the state government's image taking a beating, Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan could do little but watch as he is himself in trouble over the 'dumper scam'.

No wonder the Congress has revised its poll issues: corruption is now the focal point of its campaign.

Heading: Overworked jumbos get a break - Indian Express
Content:
The cable war that M.K. Azhagiri launched against the Maran brothers seems to have backfired on Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi's elder son.

While the Telecom Dispute Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) has posted a complaint from Azhagiri's recently-launched Royal Cable Vision (RCV) for further hearing in July, the Maran brothers' Sun Group, with a host of well-known channels and immensely popular TV soaps, is now selling their direct-to-home service like hotcakes, drastically reducing the number of potential subscribers for RCV.

The TDSAT ruling has ensured that the case will go on at least for a few more months. This isn't good news for Azhagiri because thousands of consumers across Madurai and other areas in South Tamil Nadu are upset with RCV for not showing Sun's bouquet. Cable operators have also turned against Azhagiri's network as the public has been hammering them for Sun channels.

When Azhagiri's RCV network was launched on June 9, all Sun Group channels—about 20 in four south Indian languages—were taken off air.

But things turned around due to public pressure and to deny an outright victory to his rivals, Azhagiri went to TDSAT, though with little change in the result.

"The case will take months to resolve as the Sun Group is equally powerful in terms of their financial might. In the meantime, pressure from the public will make his position weaker," said an independent operator.

In fact, several operators, on condition of anonymity, said that they were all ready to join the RCV fold, if they lift the blackout on Sun channels. "Without those channels, we will not be able to go to the public with connections or collection," they said.

The Marans seem to have won this round of the family spat. Several households in Tamil Nadu are opting for DTH systems, mainly Sun's. Sun Direct is now the rage in Madurai, with over 1,500 sets being sold in the recent past.

It is the operators who are caught in the middle. "People going for DTH means less business for us. The Sun Group is now considering RCV operators as deserters and are not ready to understand the physical and financial threats that we face," said another operator.

Heading: Ready for talks, but no Gorkhaland: Buddha - Indian Express
Content:
Tiruvalla Unnikrishnan has never quite liked temple festivals—people around him went into a trance as the drum beats rose to a crescendo. Not him. In April this year, as he stood in the sweltering heat at the famous Kootalmanikyam Temple at Irinjalakkuda, Kerala, Unnikrishnan suddenly raised his trunk and trumpeted. The drums went eerily silent and then, Unnikrishnan ran amok, trampling two and goring the third person to death. The rampage ended only after a team of veterinarians tranqualised the elephant.

Unnikrishnan had turned violent at last year's festival too. Clearly, he was overworked and needed rest. Now he has help.

Recognising that erratic behaviour in captive elephants is linked to bad working conditions, Project Elephant, India's flagship elephant programme, is for the first time setting up four elephant rehabilitation centres in different corners of the country to provide rejuvenating check-in facilities for "working" elephants and a home for "retired" elephants.

In India, where about 3,400 plus captive elephants, are revered, kept in temples, and passed on as family heirlooms, these jumbos are often overworked and denied medical facilities.

"Erratic behaviour in working elephants occurs because they don't get adequate rest or medical attention. We are creating facilities where a working elephant can check in for two or three months, rejuvenate itself and then get back to work. These incidents where elephants run amok in temples or near tourist facilities are because there are usually no facilities where the elephants can take a break," says A.N. Prasad of Project Elephant.

While Haryana will have the largest and biggest of these medical-cum-resting facilities, work has also started on one in Orissa. From the South, Trivandrum in Kerala has expressed interest, and a fourth for the North-east is likely to be built in Tripura. The Ministry of Environment and Forests has also asked all states to conduct surveys on the number of captive elephants.

Experts working closely with elephants say medical attention in different parts of India differ.

In Kerala, which has more than 600 elephants, the pachyderms are used in temples festivals and are protected by law, while Assam, which has the highest number (over 1,200), uses its elephants for all kinds of purposes. North Indian elephants are the worst off with hardly any medical care or rest.

"Kerala has a rule for elephants to be properly registered, with a mandatory veterinary certificate. Ideally, we would like this kind of stringency in all the states, but the rehab facilities are an important step forward," says Prasad.

"There isn't a doubt that mahouts and Indians love their elephants across the country. The elephant enjoys a very special place in the minds of people. But there is still heavy reliance on traditional medication and quacks and they are not given any rest. Almost all captive elephants in Delhi have problems in their feet as they are made to walk on hot roads during the day, while in Kerala, where the male tusker is a status symbol, the animals are only made to walk at night or after dawn. The rehab facilities will put pressure on the owners to avail some medical care," says Dr Suraj Kumar, an elephant expert with Wildlife SOS, an NGO which has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Haryana Government for the Haryana elephant centre.

Jumbo numbers*

Assam: 1,290

Kerala: 635

Tamil Nadu: 145

West Bengal: 120

Uttar Pradesh: 140

Karnataka: 115

*Captive elephants

Heading: Bharat Stage-IV emission norms in 11 cities by 2010, says Baalu - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on Tuesday said his Government had kept its doors open for talks even as the resolution passed by an all-party meeting, convened by the CM, to find a way out of the Gorkhaland impasse made it clear that a separate state of Gorkhaland was unacceptable.

Out of the 16 political parties invited, 12 sent their representatives to the meeting that was held at Rotunda in the Writers' Building.

The four political parties, which were invited to join the meeting but chose to abstain, were the Trinamool Congress, SUCI, GNLF and the Naren Hansda faction of the Jharkhand Party.

"More efforts should be made to enhance the standard of living of the people of Darjeeling as well as to improve the economic and social condition of the people there. Without changing the geographical contours of West Bengal, the issue of expanding the administrative and financial powers of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council can be considered with sympathy," the resolution said.

Bhattacharjee said he was not averse to a tripartite meeting involving the Centre, the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM) and the state Government, as demanded by the GJM earlier.

"We are ready to talk to all concerned and find out a political solution to the problem. All our talks will have no precondition. As far as a tripartite talk is concerned, we have no problem with that. But before such a meeting, we will have to talk to the protestors in the hills as well as the Centre. If it emerges that a tripartite talk is necessary, we will definitely call for it," the CM said, adding he would inform the Centre about the outcome of Tuesday's meeting.

West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee (WBPCC) president and Union Minister of Information and Broadcasting Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi who joined Tuesday's meeting appealed to the protestors to shun the path of confrontation and open a dialogue with the state Government.

"Confrontation leads us nowhere. It's against Bengali culture and tradition. We also want to remind the protestors not to punish the people of Sikkim as blockading national highways is disrupting normal life in that state," he said.

On the disruption of work in tea gardens, Bhattacharjee said he had already got in touch with tea planters' associations. "The situation in the tea gardens is grim and the tea industry is suffering losses. We have discussed with tea planters about the ways to get out of this situation," the CM said.

Heading: Let state agencies investigate Hari Masjid case, CBI tells HC - Indian Express
Content:
The Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways has proposed to extend Bharat Stage-IV emission norms for four-wheelers to 11 identified mega cities and Bharat Stage-III emission norms throughout the country from April 1, 2010.

Minister T R Baalu on Tuesday told the Consultative Committee of the Members of Parliament that the Ministry was in the process of notifying the rules and it would be done soon. The committee discussed 'road safety' and the Minister said all steps were being taken to improve the situation across the country.

He, however, admitted that there was one road accident every minute and one death due to road accidents every five minutes in India.

Baalu said there has been a rise in road accidents with the expansion of road networks and increase in the number of vehicles. He informed that in 2006, 4.6 lakh accidents took place in which 1,05,749 people were killed and five lakh people were injured.

The Minister said a National Road Safety and Traffic Management Board would soon be set up. It would look into several aspects of traffic management, including design and quality of road infrastructure, safer vehicles, law enforcement and provision of accident care.

"The Sundar committee recommendations to use 1 per cent fuel cess towards Road Safety Fund was also at an advanced stage of approval. A proposal to promote road safety in educational institutions was also on the cards and Rs 120 crore would be earmarked for it," he said.

Baalu said the amended Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is likely to come through by the Monsoon Session of Parliament. It would help check the rise in the number of accidents with stiff penalties for traffic offences and more compensation for accident victims, he added

"We have proposed that the enforcement authorities may suspend driving licences on the spot for up to three months in cases of drunk driving. We have also proposed to introduce civil liabilities on a driver with a penalty of up to Rs 5,000 for rash or negligent driving, causing injury to a person or damage to property," he said.

Heading: India pushing for more freight trains to Pak - Indian Express
Content: In its latest reply to the Bombay High Court regarding investigation of Hari Masjid firing case of 1993 Mumbai riots that resulted in the death of six persons, the CBI has said that the case should be investigated by any of the state government agencies. In its reply,  CBI stated that "state has got specialised agencies like ATS, STF, State CID and Crime Branch which are competent and amply resourceful to investigate the case." Additional Solicitor General Rajendra Raghuvanshi told the court that CBI is not taking up the case as it was not in public interest.

Heading: DMK, PMK part ways in state; alliance at Centre to continue - Indian Express
Content:
In a desperate bid to stabilise the rising cement prices in the country, the Indian Government is now pushing for more than double the number of freight trains between India and Pakistan through the Lahore-Attari border route.

In the two-day inter-governmental talks between railway officials from both countries, which began on Tuesday, the Indian side made a strong pitch for increasing the number of freight trains on the route from the present two pairs to five pairs per day.

The move, sources said, is prompted by the Indian Government's plan to increase cement imports from Pakistan so as to rein the rising domestic prices. India imported 63,000 tonnes of cement from Pakistan through the Lahore-Attari rail route in May, but if both sides agree, this number could more than double.

"Reducing the time taken for train examinations is being actively considered as a measure to enable the running of more trains per day," said a Railways source adding that commencing operations at daybreak was an option to increase the number of trains.

Imported cement from Pakistan is estimated to be cheaper by roughly Rs 50 per bag than the kind available in the Indian market, said Indian Railways sources, adding that Pakistan is open to facilitating the move since it could substantially increase its cement exports.

Rail Bhawan officials also said that India is pressing for introducing freight trains on the Munabao-Khokrapar route on the Rajasthan border side, but this suggestion has not yet found favour with Pakistan.

Heading: CPI-CPM leadership steps in to resolve differences in Kerala - Indian Express
Content:
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Tuesday decided to break its two-year-old partnership with its ally, the Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), in Tamil Nadu. The party, however, said it would continue its alliance with PMK at the Centre.

The decision to snap ties was taken at a high-level policy implementation committee meeting, convened at the DMK headquarters, Anna Arivalayam.

Although the Democratic Progressive Alliance (DPA) in the state had differences since its inception in 2006, the decision to part ways followed a highly provocative speech by PMK functionary 'Kaduvetty' J Guru, who had threatened to kill DMK members.

"Even after the condemnable speech, neither any action has been taken against the party member nor an apology was tendered by PMK leaders. In this situation, unfortunately, this alliance cannot continue," said DMK president and Chief Minister M Karunanidhi.

Although the experiment to form an alliance at the national level was successful for both parties, contesting elections and sharing power at the state level always created bad blood between the two allies. While DMK refused to share power insisting that it was only an electoral understanding, PMK was severely critical of the state Government, opposing several projects and causing considerable embarrassment to the DMK leadership.

After DMK office-bearers, ministers and senior leaders raked up the controversial speech and demanded the ouster of PMK, the latter's founder-leader S Ramadoss had struck a reconciliatory note, stating that the speech was made in January and the issue was resolved soon after. He had also circulated copies of letters written to him by Karunanidhi to substantiate his claim.

When asked, Karunanidhi said the letter was regarding the transfer of certain officials as requested by Ramadoss and not regarding Guru's speech.

"Making a mockery of all initiatives taken by the state Government and issuing statements and granting interviews to criticise the policies of the Government was all that the PMK leadership was interested in. To gain cheap political mileage, Ramadoss had been saying that the state Government had failed in all fronts in its two years of rule and terming the DMK Government as anti-people," read the resolution adopted by DMK.

According to sources, Tuesday's decision was a warning to the PMK that if it did not mend its ways it could cost the party its cabinet post in Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss. Though a minority with only 96 MLAs in the 234-member Assembly, DMK is not under any threat at the state level as it enjoys unconditional support from the Congress.

Heading: GJM holds parallel meet,calls for separate state - Indian Express
Content:
With the tussle between allies CPI(M) and CPI in Kerala showing no signs of nearing an end, the central leaderships of both parties met here on Tuesday to resolve the crisis.

CPI(M) general secretary Prakash Karat and his CPI counterpart A B Bardhan discussed the differences between the allies that have been troubling the ruling Left front in the state.

Soon after the differences between the coalition partners over the food security scheme was resolved, the two locked horns again, this time over the possession of the century-old Trivandrum Golf Club.

"Unfortunately there is tension between CPI(M) and CPI. But we will resolve the issues," Bardhan said when asked about his meeting with Karat.

The Revenue and Law departments, held by CPI and CPI(M) respectively, are at loggerheads over the takeover of the golf club, with both filing affidavits before the High Court blaming each other for the fiasco.

The Revenue Department of the Kerala Government had on June 2 taken possession of the club but had to return it to its members a day later following a Kerala High Court order citing violation of its orders.

While the Law Department claims it had advised the Revenue Department not to take possession of the club in haste, the latter maintains that it did not receive any such advice.

Revenue Principal Secretary Nivedita P Haran, in her affidavit filed in the High Court, claimed that she had not received any written instructions from the advocate general on the issue as the matter was slated to come up before the High Court.

The Law Department then filed a counter affidavit saying that the affidavit filed by Haran was wrong. The CPI(M) and CPI earlier entered into a public standoff on the mode of funding for the Government's much-touted Food Security Scheme.

Heading: Rajasthan Inc bears brunt of stir - Indian Express
Content:
While the West Bengal Chief Minister convened an all-party meet in Kolkata on Tuesday to virtually write off a separate state of Gorkhaland with a unanimous resolution adopted by the participating parties except the Trinamool Congress, the Gorkha Janamukti Morcha (GJM) held a parallel meeting in Darjeeling to get the demand for a separate Gorkhaland ratified by the hill representatives of 13 parties.

They, too, unanimously passed a resolution, demanding the creation of a separate state of Gorkhaland.

Those who ratified the demand for a separate Gorkhaland included the Bharatiya Janata Party and even an important constituent of the Left Front, the CPI. The meeting was attended by district-level leaders of 13 parties.

"The meeting asked the Central Government to create a separate state of Gorkhaland comprising areas of Darjeeling and contiguous areas of Dooars," GJM president Bimal Gurung said.

In Kolkata, however, leaders of most political parties denied that they had authorised anyone to attend the meeting. BJP was the only exception and its state leaders said it was in favour of smaller states.

Trinamool Congress general secretary Partha Chatterjee said Gopal Singh Chhetri, who attended the meeting claiming himself to be a Trinamool representative, did not have the party sanction to attend the meeting.

Mohan Singh Rai, a CPI leader in Darjeeling and former MLA from Kalimpong, attended the meeting but the party's state secretary Manju Majumdar said in Kolkata that Rai had not informed the party before attending the meeting.

"This violates party decision, and we will take action against him," Majumdar said.

West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee (BPCC) chief Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi said, "The person who went to attend Gurung's meeting on behalf of the Congress was not actually a Congress office-bearer."

The GJM press and publicity chief Benoy Tamang told reporters after the meeting that two political parties, GNLF and CPI(M), had not been invited to the all-party meeting. A signed copy of the resolution had been faxed to the President, Prime Minister, UPA chairperson, Union Home Minister, Leader of the Opposition L K Advani, Sushma Swaraj and West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee.

Meanwhile, the indefinite bandh that started on Monday evening remained peaceful with no report of any untoward incident. Sikkim remained cut off from the rest of the country after GJM activists blocked the arterial road link, National Highway 31A.

Heading: Supreme Court admits petition on Gurjjar stir - Indian Express
Content:
The month-long Gurjjar protest in Rajasthan has crippled almost 70 per cent of industries in the state resulting in a loss of Rs 3,000 crore to the private sector while the state Government and the Centre have incurred a loss of at least Rs 57 crore, sources said.

According to West Central Railway officials, nearly 1450 pairs of trains have been cancelled since May 18 resulting in a loss of Rs. 40 crores.

"Cancellation of trains from Jaipur Kota, Jodhpur, Bikaner and a number of stations in the Bharatpur-Bayana-Mathura line has affected almost 20 lakh commuters since the unrest began. This has resulted in huge losses to the Railway," an official said.

R P Pathak, Section Engineer at the Bayana railway station said: "The Gurjjar protestors have uprooted the tracks along several kilometres. In most places the fish plates have been removed and taken away."

"It would take at least 10 days to repair the tracks. The 45-kilometre stretch along the Bharatpur-Bayana region has been damaged at several points and the survey can start after the protests end," he added.

The Rajasthan Roadways, on the other hand, have incurred losses of Rs 17 crores. "We are losing almost 50 lakhs a day because of the protests and hope the talks between the state Government and the Gurjjar community are successful," a senior official told The Indian Express.

The residents of Bayana and surrounding villages said business has been severely affected with the Gurjjars blocking road and rail routes.

"We have not been able to travel for nearly a month to sell our merchandise and these have proved to be trying days for us. The Bayana-Mathura railway route is very important to the economy of the area as it provides cheap transport. For the last 25 days we have not seen a single train. We simply cannot afford the private transport available to us at present," said Ramdas Singhania, a shopkeeper.

"I had no choice but to close shop since the stir began. I am incurring heavy losses. I could not travel for more than two weeks. Of late some of us have hired a minibus to go to Mathura and Bharatpur," said S K Jain, a local trader. Tarachand Chaudhary, president of United Council of Rajasthan Industries, said, "It is difficult to calculate the losses. Almost 70 percent of the industries has been affected and rough estimates put the losses at Rs 3000 crores."

Heading: Congress to finalise candidates for Lok Sabha seats in UP by August - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear a petition on June 19 seeking direction to the Rajasthan Government to ensure that people in the state are not put to hardships and inconvenience during the ongoing Gurjjar protest. The agitators have been demanding Scheduled Tribe status for their community.

After perusing the petition filed by one Lakhan Singh from Rajasthan, a vacation Bench comprising Justices Arijit Pasayat and G S Singhvi said, "We will take it up for hearing on Thursday."

Raising several questions, Singh's counsel has sought to know whether agitators could disrupt public life. He submitted that the protestors have been defying the law of the land with impunity while the state Government is turning a 'Nelson's eye' towards the sufferings of the other citizens.

Blaming the state Government and the administration for defying an earlier order of the Rajasthan High Court in September 2007 to maintain law and order under all circumstances, the petitioner has alleged that the state has adopted a dubious role.

During the month-long agitation the state Government has failed to maintain law and order situation and have not been able to reign in the violence by the Gurjjar community. Police stations have been attacked, railway tracks damaged, National Highways and other public property have been destroyed openly defying the authority of the state, the petitioner said.

"Can the agitators be allowed to affect normal life by disrupting exam schedules, damaging railway tracks on vital routes and blocking traffic on the National Highways virtually holding the State and its citizens to ransom in the name of their democratic rights?" Singh asked the court through his counsel Pallav Shishodia.

The petitioner has also pleaded before the court to scrutinise the judicial approach under such circumstances when the agitators are subjecting law-abiding citizens to unprecedented hardship and harassment. He also asked whether the judiciary is not duty bound to take remedial judicial steps to protect the citizens. Last year, the SC had described a similar agitation by Gurjjars — that had left thousands stranded at railway stations and bus stops — as a "national shame" and had demanded an explanation from Rajasthan, Delhi, Haryana and UP Police.

Heading: Lalu’s dream role: neta in a Bollywood flick - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress is in the process of finalising its candidates for Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. It has already shortlisted candidates for around 40 seats. As for the remaining seats, exercise is on to shortlist potential candidates. By the end of August, the party plans to finalise its candidates for the remaining seats as well.

According to Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Rita Bahuguna Joshi, the party will declare its candidates for half of the 80 Lok Sabha seats in the state in July.

The Congress had earlier appointed a member of the Uttar Pradesh Coordination Committee and deputed an MLA each to make a list of potential candidates in each of the constituencies. They gave their feedback and recommendations to AICC general secretary in charge of Uttar Pradesh, Digvijay Singh, as well as Joshi.

Based on their feedback, the party shortlisted candidates for 35 to 40 seats.

For most of the seats, there are not more than two shortlisted candidates, said Joshi.

Meanwhile, accusing the Uttar Pradesh Government of randomly acquiring farmland for its ambitious Taj and Ganga expressways, Joshi on Tuesday called for a Central agency's probe into "property acquired by Chief Minister Mayawati and her relatives in the past one year". She also declared the party's plan to launch an agitation against the acquisition of farmers' land by different state Government departments at paltry sums.

Heading: Congress ready for consensus on Women’s Bill, writes to panel - Indian Express
Content:
Railway Minister Lalu Prasad says he will be able to do more justice to the role of a politician in a Bollywood film than the professional actors who "wear caps" and attempt to play the part. The RJD chief, who has also been bitten by the blogging bug after filmstars like Amitabh Bachchan and Aamir Khan, however, says he's not interested in "films that are only about clinging and hugging each other".

"I had told Shah Rukh Khan that whenever he is producing a film and needs anyone to do the role of a politician, I am always there.
